Question: Is Vinesh Phogat disqualification justified?
Answer: The easiest thing is to sit in an air-conditioned office and comment on how incompetent the training staff was. Things on the ground are not that easy. I was the boxing coach for my squadron in the National Defence Academy, having boxed myself the previous two terms. I was in the 48 kg category and had to lose almost 6 kg in 10 days or so. I was off fluids 2–3 days before, slept with 3–4 heavy blankets, and always had 2 sweaters on me throughout. I just climbed stairs up an down and skipped for most of the day. Shadow boxing, in between to recover. I was around 600 grams above weight in the night before weighing in. We used some dehydration pill that sucked off most fluid from the body overnight. In the morning, I could not even walk, and was suffering from diarrhea. I had to be held and taken to the gymnasium for a weigh-in. 50 grams under 48 kgs. I had 3 huge banana shakes soon after because I was dying from inside. Lost the bout in the evening but had gained almost 3–4 kgs just by taking in water and electrolytes. Things are not that easy as they seem. I have seen my juniors under my guidance suffer through the same, and gain weight immediately as they start drinking water and fluids. How else will they fight? You need energy to box. Going to a lower weight category gives you a lot of advantages w.r.t. physical advantages but the suffering and weight loss comes as a part of it. Losing the last 100 grams is the most difficult part. I have seen people ready to take out blood, go in fully dehydrated just to get there. On-spot weight reduction is not that easy. So, let’s throw in some respect to Vinesh and her staff. They bought her so far, and I’m sure they are as disappointed as all of us. Jai Hind!

Question: What are the best mutual funds to invest in in India?
Answer: This answer is dated 20th June 2024. First of all, there’s no right answer to this question. I like to rebalance my mutual funds every year or so, see if they are matching their benchmark and is the expense to gains ratio justified. Four factors that I would generally check are as follow: 1. Fund Performance: Evaluate the fund's historical performance over multiple time periods, such as one, three, five, and ten years. Compare the fund's performance against its benchmark index and similar funds in the same category. Look for consistent and competitive returns, but remember that past performance is not a guarantee of future results. 2. Expense Ratio: The expense ratio represents the annual fees and expenses charged by the mutual fund. It is expressed as a percentage of the fund's assets. Lower expense ratios are generally preferable, as they can have a significant impact on your overall returns over time. Compare the expense ratios of different mutual funds within the same category to find those with reasonable fees. 3. Risk Measures: Assess the risk associated with the mutual fund. Look at parameters such as standard deviation, beta, and Sharpe ratio. 4. Fund Management and Strategy: Evaluate the fund manager's experience, qualifications, and track record. Look for managers who have successfully executed their investment approach and have demonstrated expertise in the relevant asset classes. Understand the fund's investment strategy, such as whether it is actively or passively managed. Of course, my investment goals and risk tolerance would also be considered. Someone in their 20s might be more open to taking slightly higher risks compared to someone who is let’s say, 45 years old and looking to set up for retirement soon. I will break down the funds into high risk, medium risk and low risk funds. High Risk Funds Nippon India Small Cap Fund Kotak Emerging Equity Fund PGIM Midcap Opportunities Fund Quant Active Fund Medium Risk Funds ICICI Prudential Equity & Debt Fund Edelweiss Balanced Advantage Fund Tata Balanced Advantage Fund Low Risk Funds You can choose any Index funds here benchmarking Nifty 50 or Nifty 100. ETFs are also a good option which follow the index. For much lower risks, you can park your money and liquid funds as well. Please make sure that your Mutual Funds are under Direct plan and not regular. This will save you lakhs of rupees in the long term. Take some time out every once a year, and see how your funds are performing. Ideally you should invest in one Large Cap, one Mid Cap, one Small Cap fund, distribute equally in your early years. Keep a debt component like Liquid or corporate funds, or you can opt for some of the hybrid funds I have mentioned above. In the larger picture, the holdings of your one fund should not overlap with other funds. e.g. If one of your funds already has HDFC bank, ITC and HUL under its holdings, you shouldn’t ideally opt for another fund with similar holdings. Diversify! Happy to answer queries in comments!

Question: Why should one have a mentor?
Answer: 2010, Academy 6th semester, as a senior just about to pass out in a few months, life was great. There was flying, there was lots of studies and then came the public speaking competition. Squadron instructors decided to make me in charge, my seniors had recommended my name. Cadets from each squadron are randomly selected so that everyone gets an opportunity. Out of the 12 cadets that were chosen from my squadron, 2 were from Sainik School Kunjpura, Haryana. These two were hardcore runners, boxing champions and physically outstanding but speaking in English was perhaps not their strongest point. One of them even went and got admitted in the Military hospital faking an illness. There was no way he was speaking in English in front of hundreds of other cadets. Not that they were really bad at speaking, it was a competition and they didn’t want to let us down. “We didn’t join the Army to do public speaking, Sir!” They repeatedly stated this to me. The next 40 odd days, everyone who was selected stayed up late, practiced their speeches, the pauses, the tone standing in front of the mirror, while taking a shower, while jogging and the most fun one was hanging upside down from the bar. The two Sainik school folks tried their best, they had a sheet highlighted with different colours and they had timed everything with even pauses where we thought they’d get applauses. There were even academy based jokes in between. Did we win? No. We finished 4th, but those 2 spoke on the stage with so much confidence and swagger, it was a great sight to behold. Below, I am addressing the entire squadron thanking them for their efforts. Those two folks are Majors in the Infantry now, and they speak fluently without any hesitation. Perhaps, one of the most gratifying moments during my training. As a mentor, when you show people the right path, it’s extremely satisfying, more so because I believe sometimes we do not know what we’re capable of, and I’m so proud the two folks were able to see what all they could achieve.

Question: Are cold showers healthy?
Answer: I have been personally taking cold showers twice a day after my coach’s recommendation. It started improving my recovery and sleep patterns. I did some personal deep-diving into the topic across YouTube, Reddit, and a few free sources. This is what I came across in brief: Vasoconstriction and vasodilation: When exposed to cold water, the blood vessels near the skin's surface constrict (vasoconstriction). This response helps conserve heat and maintain core body temperature. As you continue the cold exposure, your body adapts, and upon exiting the cold shower, the blood vessels dilate (vasodilation), promoting increased blood flow. This process improves circulation and can aid in recovery from exercise-induced muscle damage. Activation of the sympathetic nervous system: Cold exposure triggers the body's sympathetic nervous system, often referred to as the "fight or flight" response. This activation increases heart rate, respiratory rate, and blood pressure, leading to a surge in energy and alertness. The release of neurotransmitters such as norepinephrine contributes to improved focus and mental clarity. Endorphin release: Cold exposure prompts the release of endorphins, which are neurotransmitters known for their analgesic (pain-relieving) and mood-enhancing properties. Endorphins can induce a sense of well-being and reduce feelings of stress and anxiety. Activation of brown adipose tissue (BAT): Cold exposure stimulates brown adipose tissue, a type of fat that generates heat by burning calories. BAT activation helps increase metabolic rate and can contribute to weight management over time. Enhanced immune function: Cold exposure has been shown to stimulate the production of white blood cells, including lymphocytes and monocytes, which are essential components of the immune system. These cells play a crucial role in defending the body against infections and pathogens. Improved skin and hair health: Cold water can tighten the skin's pores, reducing the appearance of blemishes and promoting a smoother complexion. Additionally, cold water can help seal the cuticle of the hair shaft, resulting in shinier, healthier-looking hair.

Question: What is the most amazing thing that you have ever done or has happened to you in life?
Answer: “What’s the most amazing thing you’ve done?“ The curious 12 year old asked me. Shit! That’s a huge list. My mind went back to the summer of 1997. In my grandmothers backyard, I was climbing the humongous mango tree to pluck raw mangoes with my brother. I stopped after two because the other mangoes were quite high. My uncle shouted from below,” You’re such a coward. Can’t even do that?” You don’t tell that to a 8 year old kid, you shouldn’t. Yes, I was a coward, I couldn’t protect my mother against a drunken monster most nights because I was too small. I took those words to my heart. Next summer I was climbing to the top of the tree and jumping off onto the terrace which was around 3 feet away from the farthest branch. I take things to my heart, I’m an idiot that way. 2012, when I was flying solo for the first time in a Hawk aircraft, I was all calm, but when I flew for around 23 minutes at 16,000 feet, I got a call to land back. In that moment, I realised I had never landed without my flying instructor. The cockpit behind me was empty. I shat my pants, I felt nauseated. My instructor for the control tower called me on RT, “AJ, my son, it seems scary but you have trained from past 4 years for this very day. You can do this, beta!” I took it to my heart again. That is something you should tell to a 21 year old scared for his life. “Is it flying, sir?” The 12 year old asked again. “No, that is not the most amazing thing. Yes, it’s there, but not so much. I remember around 3 years ago, I wanted to give up and just lead a normal life, and a friend told me that if you give up, there are thousands of youngsters who look upto you, who will be let down. You can’t just give hope and prove them wrong.” “Sir, I didn’t get my answer.” The kid replied. “Giving someone hope to live, putting on a smile, letting them know that you believe in them, I go to so many colleges and when kids ask me stupid and silly questions I make sure they never feel disheartened because idiots like me and you take it to heart, and it stays with them forever. Sometimes, to fly you don’t need wings, you just need someone to believe in you, and I’m glad I could do it for a few people. I feel grateful for that.” “It’s better than flying?” He asked again. “Flying solo was the most amazing feeling ever but changing lives for the good, and then seeing them grow and them coming back to me after a few months and boasting how much they have changed, that’s better than flying upside down at 19,000 feet at Mach .8.” I wanted to call my uncle and say Yes, I’m still a Coward. Coward enough to not tell him what he did to a messed up kid back then. What we say, how we behave, and how we react when someone looks upto you, stays with us forever. It can lead to a crash landing or allow them to fly.

Question: What can I learn in 30 minutes that will be useful for the rest of my life?
Answer: I have this theory, perhaps a bit obscure and cliched, but it works for me, and I have taught it to a lot of people I coach over the past 4 years. It’s an amalgamation of a lot of books, experiences, and a few selected people I listen to. 2 Box Approach You need to have two imaginary cardboard boxes in your mind. The first one is “public” and the second one is “private”. Anything that happens in your life, anything that affects you, and anything that dictates your surroundings, literally everything including feelings, financials, achievements, and problems go into either of the boxes. The trick is to segregate the said item in the appropriate box. You cleared an interview and aced it, and are hopeful.’ Your dad has not been keeping well and needs medical attention. You had invested 25,000 a year ago and doubled your money in some equity fund. Your crush replied to your message. Your landlord is demanding extra rent from next month. These are some examples that may happen to us at different points in time. Now, it is up to an individual whether he/she wants to place the said “situation” in the private box or the public box, that is not going to be imperative. In the above examples, let’s say I place “the interview” and “crush replying” in private and the rest in public. Now, the only rule we will follow is that we can never change the boxes ever, switching is never applicable. If I have placed “crush replying back” in private, it always has to stay there. That is the only rule. What this approach will help you with: Most modern-day problems that I talk about with my clients involve their image amongst others: “What do they think of me?”, “Am I good enough?” “Am I doing enough?” It’s always the perception of us by others that drives our lives. The “private” box will allow you to be self-sufficient, and not be dependent on external gratification. Of course, the trick is to know what goes in what box? I usually advise people to follow this approach for a few months, and let life teach them slowly “what goes in which box?”

Question: What are the best ways to invest money?
Answer: Before you start investing, you should stick to this one rule: “Never listen to investment advice that you don’t understand.” Always do your thorough fundamental analysis, look at the past, present and future predictions and then take a step. Once you start investing, stick to the second rule: “Never blindly put money in a tool and hope for a miracle to happen.” Mutual funds, stocks, intraday, F&O, the list is endless. If you don’t understand or have no patience to learn, don’t invest. The important third rule that will give you a strong base: “The difference between trading and investing” As luring short term gains on the market is, it’s still way more risky. “Green Color” is rare and one has to spend years understanding the game to even make a proper livelihood out of it. The fourth rule that will safeguard your hard earned money: “Don’t invest all your money in one place” The opportunities are endless. Gold, bonds, debt funds, evergreen stocks, government schemes, PF etc. Let me disclose how I generally invest. I don’t do SIPs. I do lumsump investments in mutual funds on a monthly basis which is usually around 40% of my in hand salary. This is spread across debt, equity and hybrid funds. I’m still 33 so a majority of it is invested in equity. I generally try to keep a 80–20 ratio for equity and debt/low risk funds I invest another 15–20% in stocks depending on the month’s expenditure apart from a full PF contribution after thorough deep dive. The most important factor that allows me to invest is that I created a 6 month emergency fund 6 years ago and that has never been touched so far. There’s a few investments in Crypto I have been holding from 4 years but I never even think about it. The final rule of investing, which I think most people don’t do: “Track expenses and budget yourself” You should know ideally how much you spend on each of your categories like health, food, commute, travel, household so that you can allocate on a monthly basis depending on your needs. This will also allow you to splurge money and genuinely enjoy it whenever required. I’m not an expert on investing, I have learnt most of it through my own mistakes, coming from a middle class household, my needs are limited, I don’t take much risks and belive in playing a risk free long game. PS : Before you get influenced by any finfluencer or any product they endorse, please do your thorough research.

Question: What are some of the dark lessons that life showed you?
Answer: Please don’t read this if you get offended easily. I thought I’ll share a few recurring lessons and experiences I have gathered through my 5-6 years of life coaching, getting into endurance sports, this, that and so on. 1. Feelings are not real. Facts are! What you feel today, you might not tomorrow or maybe a month or year from now. Things that stay with you are your skills, your achievements, your gratitude for life and your knowledge. If you apply this to your relationships, you’ll start respecting people instead of treating them according to how you feel that day. 2. People change, how they treat you changes and it’s normal. Don’t sweat about it. Life goes on. 3. Lust and hate are the strongest emotions. If you can conquer them, you can conquer your sanity. 4. Draw boundaries, at work, at home, everywhere. Don’t waste time and energy over inconsequential people in your life. Too many people care too much about what other people think about them. 5. You were not born to please everyone. It’s not your job, neither is anyone else’s to treat you fairly. 6. Being narcissistic is perhaps acceptable but if it affects people around your and their well-being, perhaps you should rethink about your actions and behaviour. 7. Most people reach their 40s and then think about their health, investing in good relationships. Don’t be so late! 8. 1 honest and good friend is better than 1000 friends. 9. People will hate you irrespective of whatever you do. If you’re doing better than someone, they’ll be jealous, if you’re worse off, they’ll be critical. Even you would have done the same, so take it with a pinch of salt. 10. There’s no feeling better than doing things you always wanted to. Period! 11. Question: How do I gain motivation?
Answer: It’s a delicate point, after a 2km swim, 90 km cycle going through brutal elevations, you find yourself at the 7th km mark of a 21 km run. You wonder why you signed up for an Ironman event in such humidity. [1] Your body has given up, you feel dizzy, your feet are begging to you to stop, there’s salt on your skin, you feel dehydrated despite drinking tons of fluids. Red bull, coke, electrolytes, energy gels, the sugar rush in those calories has died down. Your system does not respond anymore. There’s ice cubes inside your trisuit hugging your tummy, your buttocks, some of them have slipped through and reached your scrotum. It’s a very delicate point. You can give up, sit down and call it a day. Unfortunately, all the hours of training do not help you, it’s all in the past. You soak your head in ice cold water, pour it all over yourself. You gulp some more coke, grab a few oranges and keep running. You slap yourself once, twice and keep running. You stop, you stop those negative thoughts, and you keep running. You cramp up, you can’t lift your feet anymore, all the ice and water has soaked your feet, your shoes are at least a kilogram heavier, but you keep running. You always keep running, and in no time you’re at the finish line. The mind will always ask you to quit, keep you in your comfort zone and fuck with your sanity because that’s exactly how it is programmed to, but you don’t have to listen to it every-time, sometimes you can overpower your thoughts, cry a bit, get emotional, visualise the finish line and keep running. Fartlek Training: Fartlek is a Swedish word that means "speed play." This type of training involves varying your pace during a run, alternating between periods of fast running and slower recovery periods. For example, you could sprint for 30 seconds, jog for 2 minutes, and then repeat the cycle for the duration of your run. Fartlek training can help improve your aerobic and anaerobic capacity, as well as your speed and endurance. Hill Repeats: Running uphill is a great way to increase your endurance and strengthen your leg muscles. Find a hill with a moderate incline and run up it at a high intensity, then jog or walk down to recover. Repeat the cycle for a set number of repetitions or for a specific duration of time. Hill repeats can help improve your cardiovascular fitness, leg strength, and mental toughness. Long Runs: Long runs are an essential part of any endurance training program. Aim to gradually increase the distance of your weekly long run over time. Start by adding an extra mile or two to your longest run each week until you reach your target distance. Long runs help improve your aerobic capacity, mental endurance, and overall fitness level. Tempo Runs: Tempo runs involve running at a steady, challenging pace for an extended period of time, usually between 20-40 minutes. The goal is to run at a pace that is challenging but sustainable, without slowing down or stopping. Tempo runs can help improve your lactate threshold, which is the point at which your body begins to produce more lactic acid than it can clear away. By increasing your lactate threshold, you can run faster and longer without feeling fatigued. You can include cross-training activities like cycling or swimming to assist in increasing endurance as well. They are highly beneficial. Question: What about sugar makes it addictive?
Answer: Remember, when one Cristiano Ronaldo of Portugal replaced Coke bottles in front of him with water? Let us see why he did that. Sugar activates the same pleasure centers in the brain as drugs of abuse, such as cocaine or heroin. When we consume sugar, our brains release dopamine, a neurotransmitter associated with feelings of pleasure and reward. This dopamine release creates a positive association with sugar, making us want to seek out more of it. Sugar also affects other neurotransmitters and hormones, such as serotonin and insulin, which can contribute to cravings and addiction-like behavior. Sugar consumption can also lead to a cycle of blood sugar highs and crashes, which can cause feelings of fatigue, irritability, and cravings for more sugar. Sugar is however not classified as an addictive substance in the same way that drugs of abuse are. Additionally, consuming sugar in moderation as part of a balanced diet is not necessarily harmful. For example, a bottle of Pepsi contains approximately 69 grams of added sugar. This high amount of added sugar in Pepsi can cause a rapid increase in blood sugar levels. This can trigger the release of insulin, a hormone that helps regulate blood sugar levels. Over time, consuming too much-added sugar can contribute to insulin resistance and type 2 diabetes. Snickers bar contains 20 grams of sugar. This is equivalent to about 5 teaspoons of sugar. While the sugar in a Snickers bar comes from multiple sources, including milk chocolate, caramel, nougat, and peanuts, it is still considered to be a high amount of added sugar. Let me tell you, “Why we should not consume added sugar in huge quantities?” Sugary foods that should be generally avoided, and may be consumed in moderation on special occasions: My advice: Check the label on the food and see how much added sugar is there. I did run away from home but for some weird reason, my girl didn’t, so I was on the run for almost 5–6 days. Seemed pretty heroic to me back in the day. I also missed my Sanskrit exam. My parents had given up hope and I was preparing to repeat my 10th standard again. Enter, my school principal: The gentleman in the middle. He got my subject changed from Sanskrit to Hindi. Those days the board exams spanned over a month and Hindi exam was yet to take place. I studied Hindi for around 2–3 days and gave the exam. I got pretty good marks overall, not going to lie but if my Principal hadn’t stepped in to save my rear, things would have been different. I don’t know how or what he did, I have absolutely no clue. He has known me from past 4 years, I was the school topper, NCC head, this, that and all but he believed in me when I was absolutely down, out and had given up. He could have just ignored me and gone on with his life but he chose to stand up for one of his students who wanted to lead Bollywood-drama-filled life. Everything I am today, would have been different if not for that, and I’m forever grateful. I met him a few years ago in Bangalore, in a Coffee Day. He looked sick. I wanted to pay the bill but couldn’t dare disrespect him that day by doing so. He passed away last year due to a liver ailment. I still remember he taught us “Julius Caesar” on weekends during 10th standard. He was witty, funny and strict. Everyone was scared of him, even the teachers but he stood up for many students when the time came, not just me, for a lot of other idiots too.

Question: What are some lessons 30 somethings wish they could tell their 25-year-old selves?
Answer: Throughout my 32 years of existence on this planet, I have slowly unravelled these slightly harsh truths, most of them about people around you. Do I wish I knew these when I was 25, or 20? No, somethings you have to learn the hard way, life’s syllabus takes of these things eventually. 1. Nobody owes you anything. Everyone around you is in touch or is nice to you because they get something out of you. It might be as small as a familiar face or assurance, or respect or to prove to themselves they’re nice human beings. Only exception are your parents and closed ones. 2. Everyone wants to go to a party with you but not to your funeral. People will turn up to celebrate with you, feed you, get you drunk and so on. However, only a few will actually show up when you’re down or even realise you need help. Nobody wants your regrets and remorse. 3. People will surprise you. They will walk right over you, betray you, abandon you. Don’t be surprised, it’s part of your story. 4. When we genuinely have someone who cares for us, we will always take them for granted because they’ll show up, be there and vouch for you no matter what. Don’t lose them, you might never get that back. 5. Eventually, everyone shows their true colors. Everyone gets their due, trust me on this. Putting on a fake smile and being pretentious is very tiring, and people eventually leave that facade. If someone has wronged you, in due course they will regret it, you don’t have to plot any sort of revenge. Life and nature balances it out. 6. People who care for you, will actually be harsh on you, tell you to do the right thing again and again and be critical of you. Most often, idiots don’t understand this and lose out. There are good people out there. There are bad people out there. Question is what do you want to be and why?

Question: How do you build a habit?
Answer: Building a simple habit takes 3–4 weeks of consistent belief in an activity’s purpose and your commitment. The basic need is to believe in the “why” you need to build that habit. Sometimes, this “why” can be influenced by peer pressure. For example, if most of your colleagues love going out on a Friday to grab a drink, eventually you might end up going with them and it might soon become a habit. The “why” here is this activity on a Friday night seems to give you a feeling of relief from a hectic week of work. You might end up not questioning the “why” here because of peer pressure. Your mind tends to skip the good or bad aspect under peer pressure. So, a simple hack is to join a group or be around people who share similar hobbies or interests. If you want to start running regularly, be around people who like to run. To share an example, most people in my team were non runners, but me and another runner friend started talking to them about it. Soon, some of them attended a 5k run with us, and then many of them agreed to do a 10k with us. Even though it was difficult for many of them, they did see and experience the runners-high, and the benefits from it. Surprisingly, after the 10k, people started talking about taking it seriously, training for the next event and when we should all register for another race. Hopefully, many of them would pick it up as a habit.

Question: How do you keep yourself physically fit?
Answer: Everyone will tell you to workout, hit the gym and sweat it out on a run. Watch what you’re eating and blah blah blah…! I’ll tell you the three bare minimum things you can do to stay fit. Do these three things and you will be way ahead of the crowd. Yes, cardio and weight lifting exercises improve your fitness and endurance, I love doing them but what people often forget is that when your body breaks down during these exercises, it needs to repair itself to become stronger. The repair happens during sleep using the stuff you eat. It’s as simple as that. So if you don’t rest and recover along with nutrition there’s literally no point of working out. Let me throw an example. I’m presently doing base training for Ironman and also participating in a few running events. On September 18th, I ran a 50k ultra (7:39 circle). As you can see in my training log below, I rested my body completely the next 7 days, and did one recovery run at slow pace, a small walk and a 15 minute swim. The entire week I focused on rest and recovery otherwise. Even leading upto the 50k ultra, I was giving my body ample time to recover. Around a week later, again I started walking and running at easy levels so I could run a half marathon on October 2nd. After this, I will be going back in training mode again, resting and recovering aptly until November when I have another Ultra run in Goa. Point to note is that on all these days my sleep is around 7–8 hours 95% of the times. I never skip a meal, have my fair share of snacks and I hydrate myself constantly. This combination of training, recovery periods, rest, nutrition has increased my fitness tremendously in the past 3–4 months. Even if you’re not a hardcore enthusiast like me, just sticking to the three above points will make your life much better. Stay fit, stay smart!

Question: How did you quit smoking?
Answer: I started smoking when I was 22. It was one of those debrief sessions with my flying instructor and he just passed me the cigarette. I didn’t even think twice, literally everyone around me was smoking. I continued smoking even after coming out of the Air Force. I tried to quit many times but it was not fruitful. The days I drank, I smoked almost a pack of cigarettes and on the other days I had 2–3 cigarettes specially on working days. Attempt 1: 2015. I quit smoking and decided never to touch it again. I fell sick within a week and my body had extreme withdrawal symptoms. I started smoking again. Attempt 2: 2017. I quit for about 4 days but couldn’t continue the streak at all. Attempt 3: 2020. The lockdown helped and I was smoke free for almost 2 months. I wasn’t trying to quit but there were no cigarettes available anywhere due to the pandemic. Attempt 4: 2021. On a bike ride from Chennai to Bengaluru, I just decided to quit. I was exercising and training for a half marathon so I just did. This one lasted a good 2 weeks until I started going to office again. Around 4 months ago, I was talking to a professional runner on how to increase my speed on race days. I really wanted to improve my timing. “You smoke, and that hampers blood circulation and your resting heart rate. You will have to quit to improve.” I didn’t want to but I quit for a week after a vacation and started tracking my resting heart rate. It slowly started dropping. I had gamified it unknowingly. I was tracking my quitting streak on a no-smoking app and that further helped. I hung out with friends but didn’t feel like smoking, when people called me out for a smoke, I didn’t feel like smoking. My mind was hell bent on being fit and seeing my progress. This is the variation in my Resting Heart Beat. The initial data is not accurate so ignore it. It was around 74 when I quit and now with my continued workout regimes and no smoking it’s dropped to as low as 53. Elite athletes have it around 40–45, and that’s where I slowly want to head towards. My running speeds are better now, the endurance is higher, my sleep cycle is better, I don’t feel the urge to smoke anymore even if people are smoking around me certain times. What also helped me was, a few junior developers who used to smoke with me in office also joined the bandwagon with me. One of them quit completely, and other one has almost reduced it to one a week. Trust me, I know how tempting it is to smoke. It’s wonderful, I can vouch for that. I smoked for almost 9 years even though I was never a chain smoker but if you actually understand how it affects your body and your physical abilities, it might help you to quit. Quitting smoking is one of my biggest achievements and I hope everyone can boast of it too. Pro tip: Stress handling is better when you quit. It’s a myth when they say cigarettes calm you down, it’s momentary.

Question: What is a life hack that you think everybody should know?
Answer: I’m on the leg 3 of a Triathlon. Had a comfortable long swim, a breezy bike ride and then onto the first 700 metres of the run, I see a long elevated stretch in front of me. In that moment, I hated the organisers. The sun was out, it was humid and my legs were stiff from the 20 km bike ride. For all these moments, I have a mental list of happy memories. I just start browsing through them mentally one by one. I have around 23 of them. They last around half an hour, and during this time my body and mind go on autopilot mode. And it is exactly what I did, running slowly on that elevated stretch. My body was running but my mind was distracted through my happy memories. One minute, I was a kid travelling in a train with my dad, the next minute, I was watching a movie with my crush and so on. Live a life that provides you such memories and utilise them when you’re exhausted, want to give up so that you can remind yourself: life is amazing if you get through this small little rough patch.

Question: What life lesson would you want to pass on to someone?
Answer: We have been conditioned to gain acceptance from people around us since childhood. A very acute drawback of good parenting is that you’ll always find a way to please people by doing things they like for their acceptance. Let’s say, you really love a shirt but your spouse doesn’t like it. Most of us wouldn’t wear it so that we can gain acceptance from our spouse. The most common example is drinking. Most of us would have started drinking because of peer pressure, so that we do not disappoint our friend circle. There is an interesting term for this in psychology. “Sociotropy”. It is defined as excessive feeling of concern to please people around you and gain their approval. We would rather spoil our own peace to maintain our social image and gain approval of being a good person in our peer circle. As much as it sounds great to be a “nice guy,” I can vouch that you will eventually fade out. You do not owe anything to anyone. Sociotropy arises from a deep fear of rejection and lack of awareness that one’s personal needs can be prioritised. The first thing you need to establish is a boundary when you form new bonds, friendships and relationships. Prioritising your needs doesn’t make you selfish, it makes you a better human. You may be called a “person with a great heart” but you’ll always be running empty from inside. The lesson I would like to pass on: “Any healthy bond or relationship is formed when boundaries are set, and no people pleasing is involved.” Else, you would spend too much time thinking what others perceive of you, which is basically pointless. Nobody really cares or has enough time to dwell into what you are as a person. Only you alone can be a judge of that fact. It is nice to be liked but losing yourself in the process and running empty is not worth it. Neither people who like you or unlike you will turn up when you eventually burn out. It will be you and your closed ones. Thanks for reading.

Question: What is the most clever life hack you've learned?
Answer: Inversion[1] This is literally the most simple hack ever. I stumbled upon it while reading a reddit chain a few years ago. It is used by a lot of investors, entreprenurs, process managers and so on. Let’s start with an example. Ask yourself a question: How do I get fit and not gain weight? Seems straight-forward. Most of us can google it up and get the answers. Now, let’s invert the question. How do I get Obese and worsen my health? Answer all the worst case scenarios: Eat at irregular times, load up on food with sugar and fat, hardly be physcial, have bad sleep patterns, and so on. No when you have these scenarios, tell yourself to avoid all of these. The Brain is wired weirdly. It is easier for it comprehend to “avoid” something, then follow and indulge in something. You can do the inversion on any important decision-making in your life. How can I be a good manager? How can I be the worst possible manager? Avoid all of the answers How can I invest and save? How can I go bankrupt and screw up my financial stability? Avoid all of the answers. “All I want to know is where I’m going to die, so I’ll never go there.”

Question: Life Advice: How can I make my life simpler?
Answer: The social comparison theory states that “people often come to know about themselves by evaluating their own abilities, skills, and traits in comparison to others.” [1] Since the time our mind starts gaining awareness, we are always indirectly fed that we have to be better than others around us. Why? Well, none of us are in a state to ask that question or even comprehend it and due to all this initial conditioning, most of our lives becomes a game where we are constantly unlocking achievements that someone else has already accomplished. If we are not able to do the same, we are looked down in society and we start questioning ourselves. This complex has profound impact as we grow older and older. My whole take on this is very simple: If someone is doing better than us in life and has unlocked achievements, why be jealous of them? Let’s be happy for them and cherish their life as well. Comparison is great when we are trying to level up our own game, we can idolise someone, get inspired by them but why feel hatred when someone is better than us. I think people don’t realise how much energy is wasted just hating someone or being jealous of them. Everyone’s timeline is different and everyone’s source of peace is different, comparison only creates more chaos and deters our own timeline. If you want to be the best at something, that is amazing but why tell ourselves that we have to beat the shit out of everyone else to satisfy our fragile sense of self. For a simpler life, even when you’re comparing, don’t do it at the expense of someone else failing. Save your minds energy to focus on things that affect you and celebrate others and their lives. Don’t be that average uncle and aunty!

Question: What's some relationship advice you wish you'd known when you were younger?

Question: Has your therapist ever cried with you?
Answer: “Really?” “Yes, you’re the most abridged version of a kid I have seen. A man who has grown up but thinks like a 7 year old,” the 49 year old therapist stared down at me. I slowly slid down the sofa, locked my face onto my knees and stuck my ass to the floor. “Fine, I’ll tell you. Don’t look at me like my mother. Can’t handle two mother figures at the same time, accounts for too much drama. I guess, I don’t hate people. I have gotten good at pretending to be nice or striking random conversations. I keep myself in their shoes and never judge them but I just don’t have time to trust people again, they all turn out to be the same. Probably, I feel this rage because I have always tried to do that but no one ever really tried to understand what I feel, I know I shouldn’t expect that but I’m still a kid at heart. Maybe, I just want someone who thinks like me, understands the basics of life’s truths, to lend their shoulder, tap on my head and cheer me up. In my head I am so bloody strong, and I am but in a few moments, say those 30 seconds out of 24 hours, I want to be weak. I want someone who is not an idiot to just breathe around me and smile. My strength needs a bit of rest, I guess. Or is it that I don’t want to ever be my real normal self because they would leave or I would scare them away? Why do I feel like I need to cry and take those 30 seconds of rest again and again right now. I hate you, you’re a good therapist. Gosh! I hate crying, I usually do it alone. I don’t know what exactly I feel or what is wrong with me, I just want to be better at controlling my feelings, maybe even deleting them. I really don’t want to cry.” I cried for the next 7 minute 26 seconds. “You really are a kid.” She smirked and grinned at the same time. “You cried for 7 minutes and 26 seconds.” My therapist smiled at me. I was still on the floor next to the sofa, my face locked between my knees. “You come across as someone who has clarity, who has aims and goals, who is logical but the only thing you lack is the ability to tackle short term emotional barriers. If I ask you to walk 100 kms, you would but you would never go and confess how you really feel about someone. You’d rather bury it in and not harm others. Tiring yourself is just temporary, not a permanent solution.” She stared at me. “I get pleasure out of reaching a point when I’m physically and mentally numb. Makes me feel sane.” I replied. “There’s nothing wrong in that, but that feeling cannot last the entire day or life. You have to tackle the other stuff eventually.” “I don’t want to hurt others by bombarding them with how I feel, it never ends in a good way.” “Even if you think you’re a sponge, you have to squeeze out the water from time to time, else you’ll only become heavy. Tell me about this girl you mentioned. You can’t look into her eye, you try to stay away but fail, the good in you wants this feeling to die but the rejected kid in you is afraid you’ll hurt her and yourself. You are a pro-over thinker.” “I don’t want to hurt anyone, is that so bad?” “And get hurt everyday in turn. Lose your sleep, cry like a baby in front of me. You know, sometimes if you tell someone that you adore them, they appreciate it, not everything has to be a rejection or have another outcome. Life is not a movie.” “I don’t fear rejection, been there done that. I fear I might end up having no will to open up again to anyone.” “You’re that hyper-active kid with all the talent in the world, who’s too scared to accept what he is, who thinks it’s his responsibility that people around him should be safe and sound. Let me tell you, it is not.” “I just know, sometimes sacrificing your idiotic feelings is better, I can’t be the bad guy.” “Sacrifice is overrated, it’s how the society controls us, and no feeling is ever idiotic, it is natural.” She saw another tear drop rolling down my eye. “Take it out, I’m here.” She came forward and hugged me. “I usually never hug my clients when they cry, but you really needed it.” My therapist chuckled. “I find it so odd that I pay you to make me cry out. “Can you stop hiding your true feelings behind your dad jokes? You think your anger, your frustration, your hatred, your affection everything gets masked behind your awkward humour? You have a 5 year old child’s face, anyone can tell you what exactly you’re feeling this very moment?” “I know that, but all these silliness in my strides have become my coping mechanism. I don’t want to lose it, it doesn’t do me any harm. Also, you asked me what really made me happy and what exactly I thought in that moment.” “Yes, please go ahead” “I remember this time when I traveled the entire day and reached this beautiful resort. I checked in, had a hearty conversation with the bus boy who dropped my luggage to my room, ordered some cocktails and slept like a baby. I woke up and sat in the balcony. My mind, my body, everything was at complete peace, that for me was true happiness, and I told myself that if I have to share this moment with someone, they have to be really worthy, be it a friend or a lover.” “So, you have set yourself standards and boundaries?” “Kind of! You know when you told me I have clarity about long term things and suck at these short term emotional barriers, you were indeed right.” “Hence, you pay me!” “So, basically you’re advising me to be considerate about my own feelings and not expect them to just vanish. I should not bury them. My feelings are as important as my mental and physical health and I should respect them. I don’t have to be responsible for everyone’s sanity around me. It’s okay to be rude sometimes and it’s absolutely fine to just be by myself, no guilt is to be initiated there. I’m allowed to love, whomever I want, without expecting anything. There’s nothing more important than being calm.” “You’re pretty smart for someone who cries so much.” I looked at my therapist and smiled, the smile slowly turned into laughter. “You’re imaginary after all.” I told myself. My aura of introspection is so fucked up I have an imaginary therapist counselling me for days.

Question: What happens if a soldier loses his weapon?
Answer: Boy, this brings back memories. 6th term, Camp Torna, NDA. We were 21 from my squadron on a routine night match with our dummy SLR rifles. They were just for display and training purposes, they couldn’t fire. At one of the checkpoint around midnight, one of my course mates slept off for a few minutes while rest of us grabbed some water, ORS and changed batteries in our torch. We were a good 4 hours into the march by now. After reaching the next checkpoint, post climbing a really steep hill, my friend realised he had lost his rifle on the way or perhaps left it where he had slept. We all went back along the same route with three officers looking for the rifle. We walked slowly, some of looking towards the left and vice versa. Losing a rifle is a big deal and we realised that once we reached the previous checkpoint again only to not find the rifle there. Every single officer available rushed to our checkpoint, oh the adrenalin rush they had beating our buttocks while we lay on the ground with thin bamboo sticks. We waited for the morning and were asked to traverse the whole route again between the two checkpoints, and not return until we found the rifle. We never found it, tired and sleepless we gave up by evening. By, now the rest of the squadrons were called back to search for the rifle, and the entire academy, around 1800 cadets were planned to brought in the following day. The commandant, the adjutant everyone were drawing up plans to send search parties. Losing a rifle really is a big deal, this was still a dummy one. It was found by an NCO around 36 hours later, deep inside a trench, it had fallen of the cliff from where my friend was sleeping. Practically, the worst 2–3 days of my life. Never lose your rifle, it’s a crime!

Question: Why are jet engines so expensive? How many years does a jet engine last?
Answer: Most Jet engines have a price tag of around $ 20 million approximately. To throw in some context, modern jet engines are responsible not only for thrust to drive the aircraft but also to a large extent to power other aircraft systems. A basic jet engine has a cowling, the case that contains the components. It is designed in a way to allow regular inspection of internal components. There is a metal arm that attaches to the wing. This arm, also known as a pylon relays all the fuel through pipes. As the air enters through the intake, the mighty compressor sucks in everything and increases the air pressure. The compressor has blades inside to increase the air pressure. In a typical compressor, in such a minute time, the air is compressed to around 15 times. The blades, hence have to be extremely efficient and are made from molten titanium. As the engine leaves the compressor, it enters the combustor where all the power is produced. Fuel and compressed air do the magic here. A lot of “powder metallurgy” is also involved in making the turbine discs which is a very costly process. Once the fuel and air combine together, huge amounts of hot gas is released. This humongous energy is used to rotate turbine blades. A lot of powder metallurgy is also involved in making the turbine discs which is a very costly process. Leftovers are expelled through the exhaust system which must be able to handle the high temperature and pressure. Its mechanics vary from engine to engine depending on the requirements. Apart from this, the blades at the intake are usually made of titanium alloy to withstand debris or bird hits. Nickel and Titanium alloys are used in the combustor to withstand such high temperatures. A lot of Kevlar and various Titanium alloys are also used throughout the engine. Apart from all the raw materials mentioned, the basic blueprints, different engines are made differently. An engine on a commercial plane would be different compared to the one on a fighter aircraft. A lot of engineering effort, manpower, and manufacturing chain is utilized throughout the process, and engines are produced mostly one at a time rather than in bulk. It is a very niche skill, and labor is also costly for the same. A Rolls Royce Trent 900 engine, for instance, was priced at $ 12.85 million for Qantas last decade. Emirates bought 200 of those at $ 46 million per engine.

Question: What kind of mindset is common to every successful person?
Answer: People often walk up to me and ask about my riding experiences. You don’t just get up and go on a ride from Kanyakumari to Kashmir and complete it in under 120 hours, or ride 6000 kms in 6 days. 1. You alter your sleep cycle and slowly get used to sleeping 2-3 hours a day well before a month. You holistically track your sleep. 2. The focus is more on performing exercises that strengthen the back, shoulders and forearms. 3. Practice intense meditation to be able to focus on the roads ahead for a long time. 4. Pick up other activities that boost your endurance like running, swimming and cycling. 5. A week prior to the rides, your diet becomes restricted. You eat light and avoid diary, anything spicy, and learn to survive on protien bars, dry fruits. 6. The entire route is planned, the diversions, the pitstops, fuelling stations, all keeping in mind your motorcycle’s efficiency. We only see what someone has achieved, but often fail to see the process and preparation behind it which is more paramount and time-consuming. The smart ones, who later become successful however have a different way of looking at things, they don’t look at other successful men like we do, instead they focus on their process, their habits and their journey to reach somewhere, and what are the takeaways from it. We all dream to be successful, but only a few lay out a plan, do the research and are ready to face all consequences through meticulous preparation. “Impossible takes time, difficult will be done immediately.”

Question: Can you write a short, yet dark story?
Answer: She was like the Indian Ocean, infinite and unfathomable. Every time she walked past my cubicle and waved at me, my mind got wet. We went to a really expensive brewery and requested for a table where I could soak in her presence. Two minutes into the date, the lights went off. The back up generator malfunctioned and the waiters told us it would take at least half an hour for the power to get back. It took more than an hour and because we were sitting in the cosiest corner, there was no hint of any illumination. It was complete darkness. I couldn’t see her, and for an hour I realised that I had never listened to her before. She was nothing like me, in fact she exaggerated everything. “I have had at least 15–16 boyfriends so far but no was as smart and short like you, in fact all of them were fair, you are my first dark date. This is so amazing!” She yapped on for another hour, and then the power was restored. Suddenly, she was just a small tributary of the Yamuna river trying to survive on its own. I drank my heart out until she had to leave. I laughed at myself, ordered another drink and paid the bill. On the way home, I tweeted: I once said after getting drunk and I quote “Once you switch off the light, everyone looks the same. Darkness can bring out stupidity very easily because then they have to converse.”

Will it be right to keep pestering her like a creep? No So, what’s the best thing to do? Cherish the good times and conversations, and let go. We should ask ourselves the tough questions in life. Not the easy ones, to make ourselves look like a genius. A hardcore round of introspection would lead you to answers you have been denying the existence of, and that would in turn lead to actions that bring us normalcy and peace. Question: Why should women work after getting married?
Answer: Being independent, ambitious and financially adept is a choice everyone has the right to commit to, irrespective of your sex. Let’s not beat around the bush and accept that we live in a society where women are expected to take care of the household and as much as men are responsible for this, so are some of the women. Unfortunately, sometimes it is so deeply imbibed in a woman’s chain of thought that eventually she would be required to fulfil and run a house that she never actually dreams or sets goals and aspirations. Don’t blame men here, blame the upbringing, blame the parents and blame reluctance of a society to accept this fact. Visit any small town or village across India, and you’d hardly see women going for work or even running a small business. That would be a very rare sight. So, all of us living in privileged metros and wannabe metros can shout “feminism” all we want, we will still find women who are ready to forego their identity, their purpose of life just to bear a child and throw pretentious smiles at their in laws. Who is to be blamed for all the illogical chaos? The women of the previous generation who set examples for their daughters. I am not taking away any credit away from them. I am stating that if they stood up and asked why couldn’t men contribute equally in the household chores, why only men were supposed to be the bread earners and so on, things would have been very different. Why should women work after their marriage? To be independent and gain self respect, and most importantly set examples for future generations to come, else we can climb mountains and swirl banners and yell that women should be treated equally but no one would care because there would still be women out there who would voluntarily repeat what their grandmother did, what their mother did, and we wouldn’t want that.

Question: What are some good tips for successful online dating?
Answer: Around 6 months ago, I was approached by a startup to freelance for them. They wanted a small team of writers and UX designers to break down dating apps and tell them what is it exactly that one would need to build the perfect dating app. The project was shut down last month due to funding issues. This allows me to divulge some interesting data that we tracked over 14–15 weeks on various apps like Tinder, Bumble, OkCupid, and TrulyMadly. I will share some insights from Tinder and Bumble only as they are the most popular dating apps out there. We created two groups of profiles for the study, with pictures of real people. (Apt permissions were taken from everyone). Some of the information on the bio was manipulated to understand the general trends etc. The first group of profiles included men and women who were visually attractive according to society’s standards. (Extra emphasis on this statement!) The second group of profiles included men and women who were not visually attractive according to society’s standards. One interesting thing that we observed was that women from both the groups got matches on a daily basis except for that one profile which did not have any display picture. Other facts included: There were around 32 data points like these. We never messaged or interacted with any of the matched profiles. It opened my eyes once again to what exactly people out there fantasize about. When people say, they like a person with a sense of humour, responsibility, success, blah, blah, blah in the opposite sex, you will be surprised at how many people just look at the pictures when it comes to online dating. As one of the people in the small team pointed out in the end: “These apps act more like a justification to people who want to be told they are attractive in nature, that someone would actually take interest in them against so many other people out there.” If you ask me, yes there are a lot of success stories out there when it comes to dating apps, but those numbers as a percentage would be very meager. As much as it sounds exciting unless you fall into a select category from group 1, you would have to be extremely lucky to actually find someone worthwhile. “Online dating doesn’t suck, too many people suck at online dating!”

Question: I am feeling very low. Can you say something which can instantly uplift me?
Answer: I’ll narrate an incident which happened last year with a very dear friend. The first wave was at its peak. The lockdown had stretched beyond what people expected. Everyone was happily getting adjusted to the “work from home” scenario. My friend’s father was quite old and was staying in Kolkatta while he was in Bangalore. His father regularly required oxygen cylinders from time to time. One fine day, his father had trouble in breathing and the doctor, on phone advised to get him on an oxygen cylinder as soon as possible, which was the usual routine. However, the visiting doctor got scared looking at his father’s condition and refused to provide the cylinder or any medical help until a Covid test was done. By the time, the family was able to convince him and show his previous medical reports, his father had passed away. My friend, at that time was in Bangalore and couldn’t travel to Kolkatta due to all the travel restrictions across the country at that time. He tried really hard but after a day, there was no point as the rituals had already been conducted by his mother and sister. I was shook completely by the news. I messaged him once and didn’t communicate further for a few days. I had no clue what he might be going through. A week later, I met him at his house. He was smiling, just the way he always did. It was not like he didn’t love his dad or he was happy about it. “Are you fine,” I asked after an hour or two. He narrated the whole story with a gentle smile on his face. “It was not in my hands, I tried but there’s nothing I could do about it. Maybe Baba didn’t want me to see him like that. I will go once restrictions loosen up, but I’m sure he wouldn’t want me to be sad all the time.” I swear I always thought that I was one of the calmer humans out there, but looking at him I couldn’t comprehend how the hell was he even able to take all this and smile like he always did. We talked about a lot of different things that night it throughout I was just in awe of how we was being so brave when everything was stacked against him. Other than a few close friends, he was never shared this, he kept working so as to be distracted and honestly, he was just like he always was that night, or maybe he was too good at being strong. The more people you interact with, the more you hear their side of the story, the more you will realise that there are far more better people who are less privileged than you, suffering more than you, and yet they live on with a gentle smile. You know why? They accept things as they are and understand that sometimes it’s not in our hands to decide the events in our life, and it’s okay even though it might seem really tragic and bad. It’s part of living and surviving.

Question: What are some real life examples of the placebo effect?
Answer: September, 2010 Location: Chaura Saddle Maltara range, outside the National Defence Academy boundary wall. One Tajiki cadet, one Muslim from Satara, one Sikh from a Brigadier’s family, and a few more Hindus like me were running back from base camp as part of the routine practice towards our squadron inside the academy. It was a practice josh run, and we were supposed to finish it in under 8 hours. It was drizzling, the mountains around us were slippery and our map reader was really pathetic. We were lost within the first hour and gave up soon after. This is when the above picture was taken. We kept walking though so as to reach the squadron and come up with some excuse to fool our seniors. As we climbed the final ridge before our descent towards Khatapewadi, we saw 14–18 bright eyes in the darkness that engulfed the vicinity. There was a loud howl, and for some reason a weirdly icky laugh. We switched off our torches and sat down immediately. Some of us thought it could be hyenas or stray dogs, while some of us were sure it was a ghostly spirit. None of us were sure about it. The map reader then decided to chant: “ Jai Hanuman Gyaan Gun Sagar…” Those of us who knew the Hanuman Chalisa chanted along and started walking again. We could still see those bright eyes so we decided to skirt them and take another route. That night, cadets from different religions, some of them from different countries chanted along the Hanuman Chalisa in hopes that they would reach back safely. We reached around 6 hours late, were punished wonderfully by our seniors for lagging behind so tremendously in terms of time, but even today when I think about it, irrespective of whether the chants worked or not, we all wanted to believe it as a group. Maybe they were just stray dogs but for a bunch of 19 year olds out in the wild without weapons, they were nothing less than wolfs.

Question: What is a truth that nobody wants to admit or doesn't see?
Answer: I was doing this podcast with a friend where he had invited a cardiac surgeon. The doc was talking about his life in the US and the kind of cases he regularly comes across. There was one particular thing he pointed out during the conversation that silently struck me. “I am a doctor and I know I give it my all, and I am one of the best out there but I have been not keeping well of late. My blood pressure has been varying and that is really worrying me. I reached out to a friend of mine and he told me to start focusing a bit on my personal life as well. I am always swamped with work and the stress levels are too high” “So, as a doctor, you would know already that stress is harmful for us.” My friend interjected. “We all know everything that is harmful for us but sometimes we end up being in sticky situations. We pretend we are too strong for all these advices. We think it makes us look weak. A Doctor when sick should reach out to another doctor and get the unbiased diagnosis. The same applies to a psychiatrist as well. Just because we are out there treating people day in and day out, doesn’t mean we can treat ourselves rightly.” The podcast lasted for a good hour or so but this point kept lingering in my mind. All of us need to reach out for help and not be ashamed of it when things run amok. We need to step outside of our zone of “I’m too strong for all this” before it’s too late. Seeking counsel or help doesn’t make us weak, it only shows that we accept that we can be vulnerable and that in turn makes us stronger. We give the advice we need ourselves, but sometimes we need to hear it from someone else as well.

Question: Why are there very few IITians as ''fighter pilots'', even though this job is for high intellectual people?
Answer: Not all fighter pilots are not highly intellectual, first of all. It’s more a struggle of getting your body reflexes sharp through practice, practising the same drills and emergency routines day in and day out, revising the same concepts of flying again and again, reflex actions, super quick decision making and so on. You also have to be lucky enough to be part of a genetic pool that meets requirements such as length, leg length, sitting height etc. Yes, they’re mentally sharp and alert in situations and that’s something that is either natural or is picked up during training. Also, how your body reacts to extreme Gs is a question that you can only answer when you experience it. A fighter pilot is expected to be mentally sound, physically apt, technically sound, act as wingman or as a leader, take decisions within seconds under immense physical stress and sometimes even enemy threats. Intellectual is not the word to describe it. The perfect word for all these all-round qualities, that would do complete justification to the traits of a flyer would only be “fighter-pilot.” Also, unlike the IITs, there is no quota to become a Fighter-Pilot. You either deserve it or you don’t!

Question: Can endurance biking be used to lose weight?
Answer: I have lost upto 500–600 grams on a hot sweaty day covering 900 kilometres in 14 hours from Vizag to Bhubaneswar, all the way upto Balasore in peak July heat. That was the most I have ever lost in a day but I will advise using it to lose weight. Weight loss during endurance biking is mainly due to loss of fluids from the body and that will definitely not be a healthy was to lose weight. I don’t even think you can sustain it for more than 2 or 3 days. I always consume more calories during such rides. Red bulls, protein bars, peanut butter candies, dates, almonds etc. I usually have only heavy meal in the day accompanied with lots of water and juices. To give you some visual context: This was me in Kochi on 28th May, 2018. I was about 72–73 kgs in the morning. I left for Kanyakumari and 4 and a half days later reached Srinagar covering around 4200 kilometres. This was me in Kargil on June 2nd, 2018 around 5 pm, if I remember correctly. Question: What are some of the darker aspects of Indian society?
Answer: Arranged Marriages So, after my two failed relationships, my family took a vow to get me married. That vow is like 3 years old already but I do admire their grit and determination. Now, I understand that I shouldn’t be wasting their time but it’s something you do to keep your parents happy, you never want them to feel like you don’t respect their views and aspirations. For 3 years, I have been seeing profiles on these matrimonial sites and laughing internally. You are literally a product on a e-commerce website out there. You are filtered on complexion, annual package, height, tier of your college and so on. It’s basically like going to Amazon trying to search for a earphone under 599 rupees which supports Bluetooth and has free delivery. I’m amazed at how compatibility is measured in terms of salary packages and property ownership. Fine, I understand that financial stability is important in life, then why not admit it openly. From the last 6 months, parents have started short listing profiles and sending me their details on WhatsApp. Yeah, my biggest mistake was to buy smartphones and teach them how to use Whatsaap. Now, I get like at least 25 forwards and 5–6 prospective bride details everyday. This is what I read in one of the prospect’s expectations. Why is this necessary? Just imagine, if it was the other way around. See, I don’t blame the girl or anyone but it just annoys me to the core that even today we are sticking to 50–60 year old norms of marriage. We all preach and talk about how progressive we are becoming and how equality and feminism and this and that is an important issue to understand. Fact is, 90% or more people in India do not give a damn about these words. It’s just people like me and you who talk about it on Internet and feel we have made a change. I have been rejected because my complexion was dark, I had depression, I was not an engineer (this is 100% true!) and I feel elated I was. I never had to talk to those girls or the family and it was a relief but the 3–4 instances when I have been forced to talk I have been asked questions like: “How much income tax do you pay?” “My daughter is pursuing MD, if you pay for it, you can marry her!” “You are too dark skinned. I think that’s why your skin complexion has turned dark by all the travelling in sun!” “You had depression? I read on your blog. I don’t want my grandson to have it as well.” I just smile. My intestines and kidney laugh, my heart weeps for those idiots. It’s not really a question on how much you earn, or how attractive you look, our cliched stomach scratching uncles still are living in a society designed and ruled by them. Oh, I have not even started talking about Caste, sects, etc. Religion is a different battlefield here. Irrespective of you’re a man or a woman, our Newton-esque society has set standards for you. You better start complying with them or you will be looked down at. Getting married is an achievement you should unlock soon because your family’s happiness depends on it. Your own sense of pride, your mental health, your achievements, your flow of peace has no value in the society. At the end of day, you’re just a product which will meet the shopping filters of some buyer with no after sales service. That’s why you were born, educated, so that a bunch of people could come and eat free dinner at your wedding thereby increasing the social acceptance of your family.

Question: What did you learn too late in life?
Answer: Everyone wants to buy a badass automobile in their life. Let’s say the cost of such a car is around 30 lakhs. You can spend around 8.5 lakhs from your savings as a downpayment. You call up the bank and car dealer, and everything seems to be falling in place finally. You can finally own your dream car. This is just an approximate calculation for a loan tenure of around 7 years. The EMI comes up to around 50,000 per month. The bare minimum service cost per year would around 10,000 - 15,000 (please correct me if I am wrong) Petrol price is around 100 rupees in India right now. Let’s assume you travel from your home office every day, take your family out on weekends, go on long drives with friends from time to time, and say you drive around 1000 kilometres a month. That would amount to around 100–120 litres of petrol every month which is around 10,000–12,000 rupees per month. Your monthly expense for owning and maintaining your dream car would be around: 50,000 (EMI) + 1,500 (maintenance) + 12,000 (petrol) = 63,500 rupees. Of course, owning your dream car with your hard-earned money is a feeling that cannot be described or weighed against money, and as your car grows old, the maintenance and service charges would increase. Depending on how you drive and maintain your “beast”, a lot of spares would need to be changed. Even a tiny scratch or dent would make your heart sulk because you are still paying the EMI, so additional costs on that. I am not even talking about parking fees at every place you visit, toll fees on highways, car wash charges, and of course accessories like better navigation tools, audio systems and so on. No, I am not suggesting that you should not buy your dream car. We all should, we all should enjoy the privilege of a high horsepower engine under our rears. It is exhilarating. What I am trying to tell you is: Also, assets like a car are depreciating in nature. 7 years later, when your EMI finishes, the price of the car would be quite meagre. The interest you would have paid month after 84 months would have amounted to 50,000 x12 x 7 = 42,00,000. Investing that amount in a mutual fund SIP would have led to this: You could have cycled down to your office every day to stay fit and save petrol. In cases of emergencies, use Uber/Ola etc, or perhaps in extreme emergencies, hire a cab. This is my opinion completely. I am just trying to give a perspective here. Thanks for reading, I hope you get the point I am trying to make. Think about your long term decisions in life. Do not jump in impulsively.

Question: Could you share an interesting anecdote told by your military instructor?
Answer: My flying instructor was not much of a smoker. Most of the instructors in our squadron would assemble hourly outside the briefing room and spoil their lungs but my instructor just stood there gossiping. He was a lovely chap. Cute as a button who sang Kishore Kumar songs while doing barrel rolls in the Kiran MK-II. He never got angry and was always in a wonderful mood. One day, however, I saw him smoking along with the other instructors. He seemed stressed and I heard him saying to the other instructors, “ Don’t tell my wife. You guys always get me in trouble.” I saw him smoking a few times more in the coming months. Months later, when I was sharing a drink with him, I asked him about the smoking incident. “Whenever I fight with my wife, I smoke a cigarette. The intensity of the fight decides how many cigarettes I will smoke.” “Isn’t that weird?” I asked. “When I was in my training days, my instructor told me that smoking is injurious to health but not talking to your wife is even more injurious. He used to fight every morning with her, but by evening he forgot all about it.” “So, you picked it up from him?” “No, not really. My wife hates smoking. She has strictly told me not to.” “I don’t see the logic,” I smiled. “See, when I smoke a cigarette, I am filled with guilt. To cover up that guilt, I have to be nicer and forget that we fought, because mostly I am at fault.” “Wow, you’re a genius, Sir” “I know it’s stupid but it works. You know the best part about all this?” “What?” “I know she knows that I smoke from time to time. She’s not that dumb.” “You’re not scared?” “It’s an unsaid mutual agreement between us. Maybe it’s her way of showing me some love.” “Cheers to that, sir,” I raised my mug to him.

Question: What was the biggest financial mistake you made in your 20s?
Answer: I was 25 when I was working in a subtitling company back then. Me and my friend Jitesh had these long conversations about life, relationships etc from time to time over beer and old monk. My salary was 17,000 then. I was pretty satisfied as I was starting my life from scratch. I think Jitesh’s salary was slightly higher. Whatever I earned was spent on eating out, drinking on weekends, petrol and a little bit of contribution at home. Savings was nil. The last 10 days of the month were always spent like an unpaid intern. “I wish we end up in a job by 30 where we earn at least 50,000. That would be so cool bro!” I remember saying this to him and we both nodded. What followed in my life taught me a lot of financial lessons. Dad was in the hospital quite a few times, I tried my hand at a startup which turned out to be a fraud, left my jobs impulsively and had to take up loans to clear a lot of my debt because I literally had no savings. Jitesh quit his job soon and started his own music career. He loves what he does and I have not seen a more sorted person in terms of life decisions. After much ado, at 29, I slowly became financially stable. I regretted having no savings. Even as a low a 1,000 rupee SIP would have been beneficial from the age of 24–25. At 30, I was earning more than what I what wanted to. For a few months, I enjoyed the extravagance but it hit me that there has to be some money set out for emergencies and investments. I’m 31 now. I only spend 10–15% of what I earn. If I’m travelling that goes upto 30%. The first thing I do is invest as soon as I get my salary and other royalties. Last year, dad fell sick again and this time it felt a bit lighter. I thanked myself this time for being wise. I travel a lot, I party a lot, I love treating my close friends and hanging out over beers and steaks but my spend is always fixed. Life is a fine balance between enjoying and living like there’s no tomorrow and living like anything can go wrong anytime, and trust me it will. Start saving early. Do your research, invest in Mutual funds, FDs, think about inflation, earmark an emergency fund, earmark a vacation fund but at the same time enjoy it because you’re working your rear for it. I would have saved a lot of money if had just started saving and investing early. Think about your parents and what responsibilities you have and remember, money in the bank, is always a huge burden less on your shoulder. This is not a financial advice, this is my opinion from my personal experiences. Do your homework and understand that no one would ever respect you if there’s no legal money in your pockets. Money can’t buy happiness but it can buy you a good place to be sad in.

We had started discussing our marriage plans, the kind of investments we would do together, and so on. Life had changed so much in the past 5–6 months, that everything seemed like a dream. One evening, on another romantic date on her terrace, we were drinking wine and had ordered some food. It seemed perfect, we were discussing International relations, armed conflicts, and suddenly I told her that I would really never let go of her so easily. She smiled and then blushed for a few seconds. While leaving that night, her phone suddenly buzzed, and she gasped that it was her ex. I smiled and told her she was mature enough to know how to deal with it. The next two days, she did not reply to any of my messages, and finally, when she did, she told me that her ex wanted to meet and they would be meeting for breakfast the next day. It was a bit weird so I asked her what was the purpose or should I be wary of anything? She did not reply and asked me to give her some space. I obliged and I waited for 3 days. When eventually, there was no sort of communication from her end, I texted her. “I met him and my mind is slightly more inclined towards my ex. We broke up 8 months ago and there is a lot of history between us. I hope you understand.” It was hard, obviously, it always is. I was down for a good two days. Fortunately, I was wise enough to sit with my friends and talk it out. Everyone was scared that our inner circle of friends would break now, but I promised that will not happen. A day later, I met an old friend at his house and told him that I still wanted her back, and maybe I should talk it out. He laughed at me and threw a beer can at me. “Even if you get back together, 10 years from now when you are on a vacation, at the back of your mind, you will always remember that she left you for her ex. You were the second option for her, or maybe just a rebound. You will never have self -respect for yourself. What about everything you have been doing for the past 4–5 years. What about all that self-respect you have gained? If someone can leave you today for someone else, they can do the same. a few years from now as well. They are called opportunists.” I guess, I knew it but my mind was not ready to accept it. I never spoke to her or texted her. Deep inside I hated her but slowly it faded.
