Question: What is the history of the Israeli-Palestinian conflict?
Answer: The conflict in question is perhaps one of those chapters of History and present-day politics that might startle humanity. It is extremely difficult to point out the origin, the right, and the wrong. The more you read about it, the more you start to question the source of the information. From 1882 to the end of the Second World War, large-scale movement of Jews took place from around the world to a place called Palestine. In 1917, by the time the British took over Palestine, it announced that Palestine will be established as a national home for the Jewish people. It was known as the Balfour declaration. After the widespread horrors of the Holocaust, the case for an independent Jewish state became even stronger. The Arabs around Palestine were not particularly happy with the decision. Things intensified after the Second World War when the United Nations announced to split the territory into three parts: Jews, Arabs, and an international trusteeship in Jerusalem. The Arabs, of course, were not willing to accept this decision. An Israeli-Arab war broke out and a lot of undocumented events took place following it. According to Israelis, a lot of Arabs left voluntarily from Palestine, and according to another narrative, the Israelis forcefully began to vacate Arabs from their homes. In 1948 alone, more than 700,000 Palestinians fled from their homes which is known as “Nakba” (Arabic for “Catastrophe). However, there were many Arabs who refused to move and stayed back. After the war, Israel gained control of the majority of Palestinian territory except for the West Bank and the Gaza Strip. In 1967, another war broke out which lasted for 6 days. Israel took over control of West Bank from Jordan by defeating Egyptian, Syrian and Jordanian forces. Since then, peace talks have never ended in a peaceful conclusion. While those who fled in 1948, demand that their homes be reinstated, Israel has been adamant with its demands. In 1993, the Palestinian Liberation Organization was formed, and it was recognized as a representative of Palestinians by Israel. It was given some governance powers in West Bank and Gaza. This was a temporary arrangement which was to initiate peace in the region but that like always, did not happen. Israel’s to-be Prime Minister visited Temple Mount in East Jerusalem which irked Palestinians as they saw it as a statement of Israel’s supremacy over the Al-Aqsa mosque (holy site for Muslims). this again led to a lot of violence. Things heated up post this event, and there were thousands of casualties, the majority of them through suicide bombings. The Israelis retreated from Gaza, and a terrorist organization, Hamas, a Sunni fundamentalist group took over the territory. Meanwhile, another group known as Fatah remained active in West Bank. Hamas wreaked Havoc through rocket and mortar attacks over the Border, and this led to Israelis refusing to any kind of peace agreement. Israelis put Gaza under a blockade that limited basic food and energy supply for its population. The Two-state solution kept forward which proposed an independent Palestine state west of the Jordan river also was a failure. Israel is not ready to let go of East Jerusalem which would have been the capital of the proposed Palestine state. Three wars have been fought between militants in Gaza and Israelis since 2008. The next war is always on the cards. The problem, as I see it is that Hamas, Israel, and every small group involved in this dispute seems to feel all the territory belongs to them. Honestly, the involvement of US in this issue only makes it worse. There are only three ways this conflict can end. One State Solution: Everyone lives peacefully forgetting the past in the territory. Two-State Solution: Both the sides accept split territories, and live peacefully. Destruction: Human rights are abused from all angles, and one of the involved parties wipes out the other. We can only study and comment on the situation, and as I see it, I do not see any peace in the region for a lot of coming years. Israel is far ahead in terms of military prowess, and Palestinian outfits are too hardened by their past to give up.

Question: What is the brutal truth about relationships?
Answer: Love fades away. I swear it does. Over a period of time, all that infatuation, passion, fire and all those synonyms used by poets to describe love fades away. Scientifically, it takes around 36–48 months but it may fade away sooner or later as well. Honestly speaking, the more passionate your love is the more steeper will be the decline. Sounds harsh, doesn’t it? Whatever happened to all that true love in movies and books! Well, honestly not many pieces of entertainment actually dwell into the time period after 36–48 months of “love at first sight”. Every couple reaches a point of time where the sparks have died and there is nothing really exciting to look forward to. If you’re still in a new relationship, trust me, you’ll feel that it is not possible. What we need to understand is that the human mind works in mysterious ways and it perceives relationships as an altogether different entity. All that holding hands, going on dates, public displays of affection, making out secretively, romantic acts, dreaming about the future does not seem exciting after a while. The mind needs change constantly and if you don’t provide it, it’s going to create havoc. So, love fades away. Then, how exactly do relationships last? The mind sees any of your companionship as a romantic one or an attachment. The romantic one requires constant rekindling and it always seeks more and more. That’s why romance fades, and love gradually declines. The attachment is very simple. “I am more than happy just being around you, and that means the world to me,” is the core essence here. The good long lasting relationships last because attachment slowly overtakes romance before the time period of 36–48 months. It does not end the romance, it’s just that attachment takes more precedence. It’s like a good 80–20 mixture. So, how exactly do you grow attachment? It’s very simple. Do what you exactly did with your friends. Know them, share each other’s darkest secrets, just sit and talk aimlessly for hours, ignore their weaknesses, tease them, help them realise their strengths and so on. Surprisingly, this is on the same lines of what parents do to their children in their formative years. That’s why we are so attached to them. My mom and dad have been married for more than 30 years now. It was an arranged marriage and in the beginning dad used to write poems for mom, and now they just sit next to each other the whole day at times wondering when I will get married or just sharing some completely random gossip. They cannot survive without each other for even a day. I have seen them literally calling each other every hour when they’re apart. It’s the perfect example of when attachment takes over and a lasting relationship forms. Good sex, your partner’s body, those sparkling eyes, your intense feelings of love, and all those stupid things you see in a rom-com movie don’t really matter. The key to a good relationship is letting attachment take over slowly. Don’t see each other as lovers, be good friends and of course, be loyal. Bonus Tip: Do not go all out in the first few weeks or months itself. Your relationship will fade away faster.

Question: What is an interesting fact of history that most people don't know?
Answer: The year was 1999. While the world was preparing for Y2K and the Kosovo war was nearing anend, a tiny Asian country called Japan suddenly realised that it had no official flag and national anthem. The sun-disc flag of Japan was in use since the 12th century. The circle was not exactly in the centre and was more closer to the hoist. This was how the flag had always been in use. In August 1999, a bill was passed that recognised the flag and the national anthem. The flag was redesigned and the circle was now shifted to the exact centre. The dimensions were changed and even though there was not exactly a mention of the change in color, there were visible differences. Of course, not everyone was happy with the change in the country. It’s use was debated subsequently and the governments ideologies were questioned since the original flag was widely used by the military during the 2nd World War. Why they redesigned it when they could have just recognised it as their national flag? [1] If anyone can find an appropriate reason, I’ll be glad to hear.

Question: Why is controlling the corona virus difficult in India?

Most of us even with all the information available are still stuck in the “this-cannot-happen-to-me” state. It just makes me sad since even one infection can sprout together a whole lot more in a few days. Lack of education, employment in the present times, access to basic life necessities and most importantly, ignoring the pandemic due to lack of awareness is one of the biggest obstacles as of today. In that chaos perhaps, no one realised a 10 year old was seeing his first dead body. Question: What is the most bulletproof advice your dad ever gave you?
Answer: My dad is a typical retired government servant. His day begins with the newspaper, and ends with a dose of prime time news or “CID” He handles all the documents in the house. He has a different folder for his records, a different for my bikes, for my records and a different one for my mother. The number of folders actually surpass his age. From his very first salary slip to the letter his colleagues wrote him on the last day, everything is in the folders, and it is organised. Not only that, he is very particular about where we place the torch, the nail cutter, the remote control and a few other things as well. “Even in the dark, if I search for a document, I should know where the torch is, and where exactly I will find that particular document.” He always keeps saying that. Personally, I rely more on my memory, and I am not a huge fan of organizing things to such extent. So, last summer, my parents had gone out somewhere, and I was alone on a weekend at home. The gas cylinder guy came, and I had to show some kind of a log-book to him. I searched and searched but could not find it. I called my dad and he told me, “Yellow folder, on the right hand side with the label “household bills.” Voila! It was exactly there. My dad was PS to the Urban Development minister for more than 30 years. Never once was he questioned for his work or ethics. You know the most bulletproof advice he gave me: “Organise your things!” No, not this one. This is an end result to it. “Son, you are the most laziest man I have ever seen.” No, no this one as well. This is his way of showing love. “It does not hurt to be well-prepared in life.” Yes, that is the one. I try to follow it, but I fail more often than not but whenever I have followed it, it has always been beneficial.

Question: What's the dumbest thing you've done for someone you had a crush on?

Perhaps, I will never tell you whatever I wrote and I know perhaps you may never even read this but this is what love is to me. So, for now we are just happy that we tried, at least we will not have regrets that we did not, and as for the answer to that question, I am yet to find a solution and text back. Question: What was the scariest experience you ever had?
Answer: Skydiving at night. It was during my second term in NDA. During the term breaks, I had opted for a 21-day skydiving course instead of going home. Being a future Airforce warrior, flying up and jumping off in daylight was not a huge deal. We were trained initially for a week inside hangars. It involved a lot of failsafe procedures, emergency precautions and so on. The first-day jump was with an instructor, did not feel a thing. The second jump was solo and gave me a first-hand experience of the vast blue skies, and how it feels to be just above everyone else, literally. The third jump was a cakewalk as well. The scariest things are usually the ones which we have not experienced yet. I had no clue jumping off a plane at night would probably raise every inch of hair on my body for such a long time. The night jump was compulsory if we were to complete the course, and honestly, I had no clue that it would be like falling into an abyss. We took off at around 0230 hours, and in around 20 minutes slowly climbed up to around 13000 feet. I am really not sure about the numbers, it was almost 10 years ago. The plane slowed down substantially and the door was opened. I saw people in front of me jumping one by one shouting something which I could not hear due to the loud propellers and the winds. Till this time, I was really confident and not a single cell of my body was immersed in fear. The problem started when I reached the door and saw what lay outside the plane. Nothing! If you could picture “nothing,” it is what I saw that time. For a second, I forgot that I was in a plane about to jump off into complete darkness. It was the Grim reaper waiting to engulf me into his abyss. I jumped, I had to, I was the last one in the line. I screamed. I kept screaming. I could sense myself falling forever into “nothing.” Suddenly, a layer of haze pierced through me and then another. There was no end to it, time had stopped for me and I felt was the only man alive in this whole world. I was still falling down, down towards the earth at speeds that none of the organs were ever used to. I was scared, I swear I might have pissed, I am not sure. I wanted it to end but it was not under my control anymore. I guess that is the worst situation to be in life, without control. I was so scared that I could not even remember things I wanted to remember in my final moments. Time was still frozen. The winds were flirting with me and deep inside me, my organs had started dying one by one. Suddenly, another layer of haze cleared and I saw light. I had not even once looked at my height-indicator, I was not in a state to. With a bang, my chute opened and I slowed down. There was light below me. (Representative Picture) There were bright settlements, and it did not seem the Grim Reaper was waiting for me. From there on, it was all about my patience and my fear battling each other till I landed abruptly on some farm outside a village. I was supposed to target a particular settlement of lights but I had forgotten to navigate. I screamed and screamed as I landed, congratulating all my organs that we were alive. “To escape fear, you have to go through it, not around.”

I was taken back through the security to the main check-in counter. All this while the plane was on the tarmac waiting for me to pay a fine of 1500 rupees. I was given a new boarding pass, was rushed through the security and amazingly my name was being called out on the PA for being late even though the Air India authority was with me all the time. Tweeted to them a lot of times, sent emails, tried reaching out on customer service but it seems they have taken for granted that they are going to shut down, and they do not give a giant dinosaur’s bum. Before I end the answer, I would love to repeat the synonyms I used in the very first sentence. Air India. Hands down, the most Atrocious, Incompetent, Rubbish, Inept, Negligent, Disgraceful, Intolerable, Amateurish airline ever.

Question: Can an atheist be spiritual?
Answer: This is Mantralayam. A small town in Andhra Pradesh which is home to the temple of a saint. My entire family, especially my mother believes in the higher power that exists here. I do not, however, once or twice a year I ride from Bangalore to this place covering around 400 kilometers. To start off with the ride is really great with some picturesque sceneries. I go inside the premises and sit on my own watching everyone. It is amazing to see everyone so dedicated to a deity because they want their wishes fulfilled. There are people who roll horizontally along the floor around the deity, people who encircle the deity a thousand times and so on. I buy a packet of prasadam[1] and immerse myself in everything that is going around. Over the years, I have come to realize that I find myself at the utmost peace during this time. Perhaps, because no one around carries any kind of negativity or perhaps there is so much harmony. I do not know exactly why but it feels serene. I have contemplated the human spirit umpteen number of times while being a silent gazer. There is a common line for everyone to see the deity and then there is a VIP line which of course, is paid, and gets you a faster visit. The prasadam is paid for as well. All that does not deter me until the priests there do not allow certain sections of the society inside the deity’s premises. The saint went in for the welfare of mankind and yet not all sections of mankind are not allowed to see him. And that is when I realize that perhaps, I am better off soaking in the peace in the surrounding without any desire or wish in my heart to corrupt my faith in an entity. Yet, I will not demean or disrespect anyone’s faith as I can see it clearly driving them even though in a skewed manner. As my prasadam gets over, I stand up, encircle the temple once for my mother, and leave the premises. I walk out a step closer to the spirit of humanity, and my inability to understand it, and yet brave enough to accept that being an atheist is better if my religion teaches me to different people because their ancestors were not part of an overly enlightened society. I felt the same at Ajmer Sharif Dargah, Haji Ali Dargah, Basilica of Bom Jesus as well. I do not know if it is spiritual or not, but I do know it is peaceful. Also, you should definitely try the prasadam at Mantralayam.

Question: Have you ever met your bully later in life?
Answer: I still remember the lunch break of that dreaded day. It was 8th standard, and during lunch breaks, we played cricket using a hardbound book and a tennis ball in the class. My crush was in the other section and that day she happened to be in my class talking to someone so I was even more excited to play. Bilal, yes that was his name. He always wore the school blazer, sometimes even in Delhi summers because he thought it was cool. After every period, he visited the water cool to wet and set his hair with a comb. His lips were so fat he could have eaten two whole large burgers at the same time. He was the most physically slow person I had ever seen and yet he walked around the class as he ruled it. I had nothing against him nor did I ever interact with him. He spoke like someone had reduced his voice speed by 60%. That day, in the lunch break he entered the class and I hit the ball with a hardbound book at him. It would not have hurt much but because most of the girls were around, he started abusing me. I abused back and told him it was not a big deal. Do you remember the first time you got punched on your face? I clearly do. He punched me, kicked me down to the floor within seconds. I was crying in an instant. I cried because it was unusual for me to get into a fight, unusual to get punched and kicked right in front of my class and friends. No one came forward to stop him. I cried harder because now I had realized that I had made a mockery of myself in front of my crush as well. I kept crying until my friends took me out of the class. My nose was bleeding and I held a handkerchief to it. Bilal came out of the class and warned me again, “ Behave yourself. If the ball hits me ever again, and I do not care who hits it, I will beat you up more. You are an ugly little guy who is going to be a ****** until you don't start respecting me.“ I was 13 back then. Probably, I had forgotten it or repressed it completely, I guess. I met him last year in Delhi out of the blue when I was hanging out with a friend. He was quite chubby in school but now he was probably a little less than obese. He was wearing a green shirt, driving a white Honda Activa. Suddenly, that lunch break came back to me, and I wanted to give it back to him. However, he calmly greeted me. “Bade aadmi ho gaye ho bhai” “You have become a big man” We talked for a few minutes and then he left because he had to pick up his daughter from school. He was married with two kids. He supplied a newspaper in his local area for a living. I could not forgive him but honestly, all that crying momentarily came back to me. A few days later he messaged me on Facebook asking me to help him out. He wanted me to assist in digital marketing for a new garage he was planning to open. I did not reply back. Bilal probably was a changed man, with a family and responsibilities but somehow I could not ask myself to help someone who had punched me for the first time in my life. I keep seeing his photos on my feed with his children. I feel happy for him and somewhere deep inside I know he was also just 13 back then, probably more immature than me but as much as I try I cannot forgive him.

Question: What is your review of Joker (2019 movie)?
Answer: I watched it in the evening on the very first day, and then again the day before while I was away on a small vacation. Both the times, there was complete silence in the crowd throughout the movie. Once, the movie ended everyone applauded with utmost sincerity. The first time I was watching it like a normal viewer, the second time I was trying to understand how exactly the director pulled off such a beautiful piece of sad poetry on screen. Let me start off with color templates. As the story progressed, I realized how brilliantly the lighting schemes and color patterns were used. The only bright color you will see in most of the scenes is the clown costume, thereby pushing you to focus completely on the main character. Initially, it was just the face and the makeup, but slowly as the character came into his own, even the clothes and the colors around him became more vibrant. Before watching the movie for the second time, I also read a lot about the Pseudobulbar Affect (PBA). There are instances in the movie where he is shown to be partially schizophrenic and depressed in general due to his general upbringing, including repressed memories from his childhood which had buried deep down. All these are in theory, the trigger that eventually leads to PBA. It was wonderful how the scriptwriters connected everything and made it logical enough for the audience to believe that he was, in fact, suffering from a condition where he laughed uncontrollably. Usually, movies that make you think after it has ended have the most impact on a viewer. This was definitely, one of them. Both the times when I came out of the theatre, I was pondering over his relationship with his mother, how lonely he was that he had to visualize someone being with him, and how so many other people connected to him in Gotham. Of course, Gotham has always been portrayed as a city that is in dire straits, and yet every single future action was justified by a scene or a snippet in the movie whilst it was exploring Arthur Fleck’s character. I was also pleasantly surprised as to how the writers did not go with the origin story that I had read in comics which was partially shown in Suicide Squad. Here, the character is a laboratory worker who becomes the Red Hood (a masked criminal) to steal a million dollars from his employer and retire. He falls into a vat of chemical waste when his heist is thwarted by Batman, emerging with bleached white skin, red lips, green hair, and a permanent grin. [1] The story presented in the movie actually justifies his future relations with Batman, and how he might have probably met Harley Quinn whilst in Arkham Asylum. His legacy as a villain was just nurtured and kudos to the writer for that. The choreography also speaks volumes about how the character on screen is trying to let go of his frustrations and just be free, and my oh my, add the retro songs that they chose to make it completely come alive. Everyone is admiring Joaquin for his portrayal of Arthur Fleck, but I believe even the supporting cast was great. Murray, I will never forget that name! Frances Conroy, the mother who probably was not what she seemed. And how I can forget the midget who probably gave us the only genuine laugh throughout the movie. The timeline portrayed by the sets is bang on and as I mentioned earlier, so are the color templates used. And just to reiterate, how much Joaquin went through for this movie, here is a small glimpse. Watch it if you have the courage to see something so depressingly beautiful, that it might make you more empathetic towards the mentally ill. Watch it you want to see what art in motion is, watch it if you want to see one of the best movies of our times. “Their morals, their code; it's a bad joke. Dropped at the first sign of trouble. They're only as good as the world allows them to be. You'll see- I'll show you. When the chips are down these, uh, civilized people? They'll eat each other. See I'm not a monster, I'm just ahead of the curve.” And if I forget, this movie surely makes Heath proud.

Question: What are some interesting Indian Army stories?
Answer: We all would have read stories and incidents of Indian soldiers, their bravery and valor. It is a fact that their commitment to the nation and their work ethic is unparalleled. Let me share a fact about the army that most people would not have heard, and honestly, a very few people would actually expect them to do the same but nonetheless, they did. The Siachen Glacier generates about 250 tons of garbage. At heights of 20,000 feet, disposing of garbage is a big issue. Additionally. the bio-degradable ones hardly degrade at sub-zero temperatures. To tackle the same, a plan was initiated by the Indian Army beginning January last year. More than 130 tons of waste was collected from January last year and was disposed at Nubra Valley in coordination with the civil authorities. The disposing mechanism, in turn, has started converting the garbage into manures for the nearby villages, and the non-degradable ones have been sent to incinerators. How exactly is this being done? A standard Operating Procedure (SOP) has been issued that each person will carry 10–12 kgs of waste every time. This becomes more pertinent because of every single source of food, ammunition, and even the most miscellaneous object becomes garbage at high altitudes. Mind you, all this waste has to be carried on foot, as there are hardly any accessible roads from Siachen to Nubra, and the Siachen Glacier itself is around 76 kilometres.

Question: What has life taught you recently?
Answer: The Rejection Paradigm I took my mother out for shopping since a festival was coming up. Honestly, I hate shopping with my mother because she will roam around the entire market for an hour, bargain at every shop, and eventually end up buying from the very first shop. I never understood what is the satisfaction mothers get when they save 5 rupees via bargaining. She took around two hours, and finally the epic act of “purchasing vegetables and flowers” was over. My mother obviously saw the frustration on my face and smiled at me. “How do you manage to get rejected at every shop, and then go onto the next one and do the same act of bargaining relentlessly?” I asked as I mentioned the OTP to the cab driver. “You do not understand the value of money, my son,” she said it with such conviction that I actually felt ashamed for a while. My mom went on for the next half an hour because I was trapped inside the cab with her. “I know you think bargaining is cheap, but there was a time when your father was not this financially stable. Every penny I saved was like gold. You have no clue how much happy it made me. What will happen if some random vegetable vendor rejects my price? He is only making me used to rejection. I would have saved at least 500–600 rupees every month and back in the 90s, that was a huge amount. If I was not adamant and feared some silly rejection, you would have never got most of the stuff you had in your childhood.” And then she threw in the standard dialogue template of every mother ever. “You will understand when you will become a parent.” It is crazy how most of us fear rejection, and due to that, we do not end up pursuing so many things we ought to have done. Right from romantic relationships to ideas in our mind that we think could disrupt the market. I believe every act of rejection makes us stronger mentally. Rejection is not a curse to be feared of, it is a dose of immunity that provides us opportunities to express ourselves more and eventually implement them. Get rejected as many times as you want as soon as you can. Someday, you will reject rejection. You may be a mother trying to bargain or an entrepreneur pitching his idea, a normal guy proposing your crush or a student applying for a prestigious college, whoever you are, understand rejection is normal, and it might be a blessing in disguise!

Question: Can Alcatraz Dey share his experience of creating an Indian record of 6,300 kilometers in 6 days on a motorcycle?
Answer: 10th August 2019 to 16th August 2019 Bangalore - Kolkatta - Delhi - Mumbai - Bangalore 6300 Kilometres In terms of hours, 158 hours (6 Days & 14 Hours) is what it took us to traverse across the Golden Quadrilateral. We had been planning the ride for almost 4 months and we wanted to set a benchmark for Indian bikers. So, we decided to do it in the fastest time possible! A lot of people had claimed on Youtube and elsewhere that they had done the entire ride in under 100 hours. I realized just looking at road condition and the extreme climate variations that it was impossible to do it under 100 hours. So, if we did it, we would be the first ones to do it in such a short time. We set ourselves a realistic target of 144 hours. Below are excerpts from blog entries on a daily basis. Day 1 We began from Bangalore onto Chitoor and we were to hop onto the golden quadrilateral from Naidupeta. What can I say, the roads were horrible till we hit Naidupeta. From there on it was a breeze until we hit Vijayawada. Gosh! The traffic in Vijayawada and the road from there onto Vishakapatnam was nothing short of horrible. Never seen such irresponsible drivers driving on the highway in the opposite direction. Looking at the roads, we decided it was not safe to drive further. For now, we stand at 861 km on Day 1. Hope is there would be no rains, no horrible roads and not this kind of humidity. I’m sure I lost about a kilo today and so did my partner Vaivaswatha. However, the bike was pure gold, the throttle to engine response time is just out of this world and honestly, I believe this bike is overpowered for Indian highways. When the highways were empty we touched 140 kmph constantly but we hardly could maintain an average speed of 70 kmph other times. Day 2 Today was supposed to be the most testing day and we knew it from before! The coastal humidity, dust, and bad roads made it the worst possible day for us. Having crossed Vizag by 1000 hours we struggled with heat and humidity and were constantly stopping to hydrate ourselves. We entered Orissa by 1400 hours and somehow pushed ourselves to reach Bhubaneswar in under 2 hours but then it started raining and the Balasore Highway from there just kept worsening. No proper signboards, lots of potholes and construction all along meant we could only cover some 70 km in 2 hours. We decided to call it a day in Bhadrak having covered 800 km more. The most hard-earned 800 km of my life. Tomorrow, we set foot in Bihar hoping to reach Allahabad and resting our souls along the Ganges. Day 3 It just keeps getting better. From the loudspeakers on autos to Shiv Bhakts walking on the road and the little bit of off roaring we had to do to avoid Ranchi traffic, and of course the beautifully pathetic roads of Bengal. Today we pushed ourselves and all my running and back exercises came into play. Now we’re in the mood and the groove to go further and faster. I keep reminding myself that this is a marathon and not a race and hence we cruised today as if nothing else in the world mattered other than me and my bike. From cows sleeping on the highways to no roads, we saw it all! Perhaps this was the worst road possible but we stretched our limits. The bike was in sync with me and the environment. Things happened as if they were meant to be! Tomorrow we step onto Varanasi and then Yamuna express highway to conquer Delhi! Today we covered 1168 km and now stand comfortably. Hoping for dust-free and pothole-free roads now! Day 4 We started off from Gaya and all the way up to Mughalsarai we suffered through diversions and diversions and we were hoping to cross Varanasi peacefully but we faced the longest traffic jam ever on a highway. 22 km of red-colored road on Google maps and we just thought of giving up but there was no other option. We saw kilometers of trucks standing on the other side and somehow through muddy side roads, inner roads and some resolute bike penetration we killed the traffic in around 3 hours. It was horrible and sucked the energy out of us until we hit Rai Bareilly and Lucknow was an hour ago. After there it was all the expressway to Agra! 300 kilometers in 4 hours flat and we stopped as rain struck us heavily again. Not a bad day with 850 km today! Day 5 We covered around 993 kilometers today touching Delhi, Jaipur, and Ajmer on the way. Today was more about cruising and we did it with patience and lots of water! The same old story of cows and ill-mannered vehicles on the road continued else we could have done more but for now, I am happy! The roads from Delhi to Jaipur were smooth and except for a few diversions along the way after Ajmer, we were able to sail through. We regularly stopped today to hydrate ourselves and had some yummy food after a long while in Jaipur. The bikes are holding good except that we had to change the coolant a few times thanks to the weather and of course the stress on the engine. Tomorrow we enter Gujarat and then Maharashtra via Vapi where our final hurdle awaits us in the form of NH 4 which might be deteriorated. It’s homecoming run on familiar grounds where I have traveled so many times. Day 6 Rain, rain, go away! We got drenched in heavy rain for almost 6 hours from Udaipur all the way up to Gandhinagar. It took us a good 2 hours more to hit Baroda where Avadhesh Khanna (अवधेश खन्ना) was waiting for us. We needed to dry ourselves and fill our tummies but deep inside I was proud that we had made through the Aravalli mountains through a thunderstorm not stopping even once. It took balls of foam alloyed with steel. When we left Baroda, it started raining again, and up till Bharuch, we got drenched once again. From there, the roads were good and the traffic was null. We have covered another 1000 km today and stand with the last 900 km in front of us. It’s time to get home, folks! The Final 12 Hours We made it to Bangalore at around 2000 hours on 16th August 2019. 6223 Kilometres, 158 Hours and Lots of Memories Later! We started off not even knowing if this was possible. Indeed it was because we believed. The route looked luring but just the distance was enormous. These are the cities we touched along the way! Chitoor-Tirupathi-Ongole-Vijayawada-Rajahmundry-Vishakapatnam-Berhampur-Bhubaneswar-Cuttack-Bhadrak-Balasore-Kolkata-Bardhaman-Gaya-Varanasi-Allahabad-RaiBareilly-Lucknow-Agra-Delhi-Jaipur-Ajmer-Udaipur-Bhilwara-Gandhinagar-Ahmedabad-Baroda-Surat-Mumbai-Lonavla-Pune-Satara-Kolhapur-Belgaum-Hubli-Davanagere-Chitradurga-Bangalore! For now, it all seems bleak, the body is tired and the bike is calmly resting but I can rest assure that this will not be the last ride we ever take. There are many more miles and places to get to across the world. For now, with a sore bum, a sore wrist, and a numb mind, I say thanks to everyone who believed and followed our ride. It was one hell of an experience! So, to answer the question, yes we did travel on the Golden Quadrilateral and in the fastest time possible![1] Along the way, we were raising awareness for the Bharat Ke Veer app which allows one to directly contribute to the martyr’s family. More than 350+ people contributed during the ride and I am sure many more will continue to do so in the future as well. We have also submitted all proofs and documents of the ride, and soon the record will be conferred upon me and my friend who took the ride. Jai Hind!

Question: What's your writing process (for fiction)?
Answer: People would think for a writer who has written 3 novels and several short story collections, writing would come naturally without disturbances and hindrances. Yes, it does most of the times but sometimes the ink from the pen just does not flow, it spills and that is where I suffer because I cannot sleep when I know I cannot write. Honestly, writing is not a process for me, it is a routine, I have to write daily to keep my sanity in check and that is how it has worked from the past 6- 7 years. I work on multiple projects at the same time, and that keeps the rut out of the “routine”. If I have no creative mojo flowing I end up writing something fictional here or on my Instagram account. I find it alarming that writing is more of a commercial venture these days for most new writers. I see most of them coming up with a WordPress blog when the writing bug bites them which has an overly fancy and depressing name to it and then they never even bother updating it. The few who do go onto write a full-fledged novel get fed up by the publishing industry within some time and give up. The few who can afford to hire a publisher, a good editor, a good designer never get the ROI they expected, and that is where the fault lies. For me, writing is heavenly, even if I cannot sell my script or short story, I would still write daily because it makes me who I am, I will never give up and to reiterate why: I do not see writing as a process, it is like having my 3 meals, my daily dose of sound sleep to me. I make sure I am utterly honest to the entire gut-wrenching routine day after day. The research, the back plotting, the narrative is what drives me in life. When I see a badly written show, I imagine myself at the story table on how the writers would have gone about the whole narrative idea, and obviously, when I see something glorious, I silently admire how the writers knitted such a tight plot. You observe you learn, you deduce, you feel, and you bleed yourself on paper every day to write without any thoughts of ROI. The best of the writers write because they feel the need to, not because their publisher wants them to write another one because they want to sell more books (part of the reason why most sequels in the entertainment industry end up being bad). There is no process to writing, you just need the creative freedom. If you tickle an honest writer during in his writing-zone, you might end up being one of the shady characters in his story. “If you want to be a writer, you must do two things above all others: read a lot and write a lot.” ― Stephen King

Question: What is the best thing that you changed about yourself?
Answer: On our way back from a road trip to Pushkar to Delhi, our car broke down near Neemrana. I was with two of my friends and the car’s battery had completely drained out. We got the mechanic and everyone possible but were unable to figure out what exactly had happened. The car just wouldn’t start. My two friends were extremely tensed and annoyed. I was just standing on the highway smiling at the traffic that passed by us. “That could have been us. In our homes tucked up in bed but we are here. The night is spoilt.” My friend started blabbering. I smiled at him and replied,” So?” “Is there something wrong with you? We are in deep trouble and you act like as if nothing happened.” “If I act tensed, will the trouble fade away? I will only waste time and energy.” He obviously did not understand. An hour later we ascertained that the alternator was not functioning properly and hence the battery was drained out. We walked for a few miles and got a guy to charge the battery. He said a minimum of 12 hours would be required so we told him to take the battery and charge it. We found a small roadside dhaba and parked the car there. Ordered food and ate our hearts out. My friend had booked an outstation cab by now and we were waiting for it. “You were right. There was no point wasting my time and energy. I actually enjoyed this experience.” My friend told me out of the blue. “When it’s over, we end up enjoying.” I replied. “You and your philosophies…” and we both laughed. The best thing I have learn is “to chill” in life. Be calm and normal in all situations. I try to be most of the times but sometimes I cannot and I am sure the older version of me would have reacted very impulsively and strongly in such situations. Mistake after mistake, I have realised there’s no point stressing out for things which are not in our control. If someone wants to leave, let them go. If something breaks, buy a new one and if you can’t, let it go. If something unfortunate happens, stop cribbing and find a solution if you can. Be calm, be zen. If you’re at peace, you’re a winner now, today and tommorow.

I was best Air Force Cadet In Ground Subjects, Flying and Academics when passing out. Studying and grasping new topics was easy for me because I was always in the groove. I knew how to manage my time and study productively. When I came out of services, I had no useful degree, but I started taking online courses. I studied creative writing, social media marketing and even human psychology. All through these online courses, I knew I had to gain new skills to gain employment again. My marks and ranks of the past didn’t matter but fact was that my basics were always strong. So picking up any new skill and understanding it came naturally to me. Today I am a narrative designer who creates crosswords, game narratives and is studying game design on his own. The point is I’m trying to make is that even though your marks won’t matter in the end, your ability to learn new skills will and that will only happen if you have always been keen to learn new thing so and excel at them. Nobody cares how much you score but they do care what skills you have and skills only come when you understand a thing inside out, and for that your brain needs to be conditioned to grasping things. So when someone says marks don’t matter, don’t believe them. In the long run it doesn’t, but you can’t do well if you haven’t trained your mind to do so again and again. You cannot run 10 kms on the first day. You need to go step by step. And to give your best time on it, you need to be running without fear for a long long time. You cannot just wake up and say, I’ll run till I die. This is not Forrest Gump, this is life and here experience and efforts matters. — From The Guy in the picture above

Question: Do secret agents fight like they do in movies?

A friend who was posted in and around Nepal had picked up the language and accent three months prior to his tenure started. Trust me, being a spy is glamorous only on screen. In reality, every inch of your soul is questioned for every action you take. Movies portray it wrongly, a spy’s job is to be undercover come what may because his life is always at stake. Question: What are the most inspiring short stories?

And all these years, I was under the impression it was named after Japanese wrestlers. Sumant Moolgaonkar He passed away in 1989, but his legacy still lives on and I guess the reason is that he was inspiring to an entire generation of automobile enthusiasts through his dedication and simplicity. What more can be proof of his achievements after his death, Tata named a car after him and a young 27 year old decades later can’t stop talking about how much he admired him.

Question: What is the 'why me' moment in your life?
Answer: It is the same old feeling that grabs me from within again and again. I check my bag to see if I have my sleeping pills, and they are staring back at me as they have been from the past 3 years. I look up to see the vast expense of blue foreshadowed by sultry mountains that never sleep, just like me. 36 kilometers from Diskit Monastery where I slept the last night and a good 5 hours from Leh, I find myself in familiar territory. The headaches are back and everything is burning inside, my epidermal skin, my dreams, my intestines, my hopes, my lungs, my soul, my bones and most importantly, my thoughts. Bike rides in the Himalayas are not a good thing to pursue when you are mentally sick and adamant not to take any sort of medication. Looking at the river in front of me, I am baffled. I have been riding from the past 6 days continuously. It is a blessing when you’re an insomniac, you don’t need to sleep much even though your body is like a living morgue which has been broken into umpteen times. This moment right now feels like a love letter I had written to someone but forgot to mail. Dust-filled fingernails, gasoline stink on my shoes, and hair that have not seen daylight since I lost the feeling of feeling anything. You would wonder what exactly am I trying to portray. Is it my solitude that I detest, is it my pain that I am running away from or the inexplainable thoughts in my mind that have made me mentally sick? Or perhaps it is a potpourri of everything. Did I really deserve to be here in this moment like a shattered show thrown out in the trash can? I just rode across the country creating a national record, and still, I feel like nothing has changed in the fabric of dilapidated life. The river flow chirps in my mind and reiterates the fact that I had lost the one person who truly understood me, who had peeked inside my pierced body and understood there was a small child hiding inside me. It is gut-wrenching to know that perhaps no one will ever have the courage or the intellect to make me feel at home again. “Why me?” I threw a stone into the river, it plopped on the bank and bounced back. The skies above were just a mere reflection of how I was exuding darkness inside my mind. I had killed my ego, I had killed my memories, my love, my humanity and I felt like a thorn in everyone’s life. “Why me?” I could not stand to be at one place for too long, my sadness would have ransacked the aura there so I started my bike again. I went to where the road took me. It was necessary at that point of time to be in motion. 6 months later With time, you get used to the agony inside you. Your body, your mind, and your pain they all merge into a single entity. It does not seem like a burden anymore. I looked sick in the mirror, physically and mentally. By now, I had stopped trying to find someone who would understand me. Someone had suggested me self-love is the only way to get out of this rut. I laughed and used the F word a few times in my mind. The problem is when you really love someone or something so deeply and suddenly lose it, you miss the feeling of loving altogether. I cannot love myself, and no it is not like I hate myself, my ego can probably crush all your mojo a billion times. I needed to love someone or something and so I did. The roads, the roads that divert from those roads, the hills on those roads, the tea shops on those roads, the smaller roads that led to the beaches, the roads where there were no roads and so on. They understood my demons, my inhibitions, my weirdness and my burning desire to love something. I came out of my thoughts when they announced my name on the stage, I was speaking in a huge auditorium about my travel experiences and how loving something so passionately had changed my mind. 70,000 kilometers and numerous backstabbers later, you may call me insane but have an answer to the question I asked myself 6 months ago. “Why me?” I am meant for greater things, to explore and to live like a nomad who knows what is agony and pain so that he can smile back at every junction when he sees someone who just needs a smile to make his day. Even though the shrouds of sadness may never disappear, I have learned to disguise myself in cloaks of wisdom borrowed from what I suffered through when I was enchained. “Why me?,” for how else I would be this badass, dear life!

Question: If a movie was to made on APJ Abdul Kalam, how would it begin?
Answer: 11 May 1998 60 kilometers from Pokhran, a spice merchant, and a tea shop owner are arguing over whether India should have mobilized their troops or not in their Rajasthani accent. The tea in their hands is steaming hot and yet the high temperatures outside the small tea shop overlooking the desert cannot stop them from striking an argument over tea. A minute later, as the background music slightly increases in tempo and intensity, their teacups start shaking and the spice merchant spills the tea all over his slippers. He curses the gods above and in the very next second feels a shockwave so intense, the weak asbestos roof overhead flies away. The camera slowly pans above, and a quaint voiceover is heard. An old Tamilian in his eighties is heard narrating as the camera quickly zooms above towards the epicenter of the shockwave. “I remember that day very clearly but I think with age, I have slowly started to forget the exact sequences of that day. Age does that to you, I guess but one thing I have not forgotten is that they call me the Missile-Man of India.” The camera in drone mode slowly flies to a town near Ramanathapuram, Tamil Nadu. “Today is 15th October 1931. I am sure it is. I am still not that old to forget the day I was born. My father owned a small boat and took Hindus across to Dhanushkodi from Rameswaram. My childhood was without questions of what religion I belonged to. Seeing a Muslim father helping out Hindu devotees was pretty normal, and I have thanked him in my heart so many times for bringing me up in such circumstances.” The camera pans over to the eastern side of India to Shillong. “I am not a huge fan of time-travel but it is necessary at this point. Today is 27 July 2015. I am at the Indian Institute of Management, Shillong. Somehow, people love calling me to institutions to address students. I never deny because I am disturbed by whatever I have seen in my lifetime in this country. Religious disturbances disturb me, and the only way to curb this is by addressing the youth to strive in the right direction as my father did.” The camera pans over to the backstage, the narrator is now seen speaking to the students but the narrator’s voice overlaps. “I was to address the students on the stage today but I couldn’t. I had to be rushed to the hospital after I felt uncomfortable climbing a set of stairs. What you see is what I wanted to do today.” The scene changes to 2030. Newspaper clippings are shown indicating literacy rates are at an all-time high. Nuclear reactors for energy have been set up across the country and an article reports that there have been no religious disturbances in the country from the past 10 years. “This is what I wanted my country to be. I strived for it as a scientist, a president and as an ordinary citizen. My name is Avul Pakir Jainulabdeen Abdul Kalam, I was an ordinary Indian citizen who left behind some books, a veena, a few clothes, a laptop, and a legacy that I hope will be picked by everyone who is listening to my story.” The screen goes blank. The title appears. “Even though I may not be more, this is my voice inside all your hearts…” A P J

Question: Who was Nathuram Godse?
Answer: Let us all be brave enough to die the death of a martyr, but let no one lust for martyrdom. M.K. Gandhi Born on 19 May 1910 Vinayak Vamanrao Godse was a postal employee in Baramati, Pune district. He was married to Lakshmi and had three sons and a daughter. All the three sons had died during infancy and Vinayak feared that his lineage had been cursed. Vinayak had a fourth son and named him Ramachandra. Fearing the curse on his family’s male children, Ramachandra was raised as a girl child. His nose was pierced and he was made to wear a nose ring, as is the tradition in most Hindu families. Ramachandra posed as a girl for his first few years of life. A nose-ring is translated as ‘nath’ and it was because of this fact that he earned his name, Nathuram which literally means Ram with a nose-ring. Soon, Nathuram had a younger brother and that is when he stopped posing as a girl. [1] Growing up, he was sent to live with his aunt in Pune so that he could study in an English-medium school. Growing up, he was highly influenced by the teachings of Gandhi and respected him genuinely. Soon, Nathuram dropped out of High School and joined Rashtriya Swayamsevak Sangh (RSS) to become an activist. He went on to start a Marathi newspaper for Hindu Mahasabha[2] which was titled Agrani and later renamed as Hindu Rashtra. By this time, his inclination towards Gandhi had started to flutter. he had started believing that Gandhi was not concerned about the Hindus and most of his interests were anti-national in nature. He started working with M.S. Golwalkar, who later became the RSS chief. Both of them translated the book “Rashtra Mimansa” into English. However, Golwalkar took the entire credit for the translation and both of them fell apart. He went on to form his organization called Hindu Rashtra Dal. In between, he was arrested a few times for political crimes and served a prison sentence. Once he came out of prison, he started reporting crimes on Hindus as a journalist during the riots of the 1940s. Honest disagreement is often a good sign of progress. M.K. Gandhi A year before Independence in 1946, he had a fallout again with most of the leaders of RSS, as he felt that they softened their stance on the partition. He was particularly not happy with the outcomes of the partition of India. Post Independence, when war broke out between India and Pakistan, Indian leaders had withheld a payment supposed to be given to Pakistan. The leaders did not want to finance a country which was waging war at them. Gandhi opposed the decision and went on fast-unto-death until the Indian leaders decided not to withhold the payment to Pakistan. The government soon reversed the decision and this irked Godse and his colleagues. Godse believed Gandhi was clearly hurting India’s policies and was controlling the government indirectly. In a desperate measure to avert Gandhi’s further interference, Godse and his accomplice, Narayan Apte started tracking Gandhi’s movements and purchased a Beretta M1934. 20 January 1948 Godse attempted to assassinate Gandhi in Birla House, Delhi. A grenade was thrown at Gandhi from the crowd creating chaos amongst the crowd. The plan was to throw a second grenade at Gandhi on the speaker platform but Godse’s accomplice, Digambar Badge lost courage and ran away with the crowd. Godse and his accomplices escaped but for one, Madanlal Pahwa. We may stumble and fall but shall rise again; it should be enough if we did not run away from the battle. M.K. Gandhi 30 January 1948 Godse shot Gandhi three times in the chest with his Beretta. Herbert Reiner Jr., a young consul at the American embassy was the first to grasp hold of Godse by the neck and later got him arrested. Godse was put on a trial in Punjab Court. Although there were pleas from Gandhi’s two sons to forgive him, it was rejected by the government. He was hung in Ambala jail soon after. You can chain me, you can torture me, you can even destroy this body, but you will never imprison my mind. M.K. Gandhi 15 November 1949 Who was Nathuram Godse? Some Indians call him a terrorist, some call him an extremist, some call him a saviour, some call him anti-national but who am I to analyse or judge. I’m just a story-teller.

Question: What has been your most heart-wrenching experience as a mentor which you can share?
Answer: I always take permission from people I mentor, and if they are comfortable, I like sharing their stories to inspire others but this time I did not feel like. It was September of 2018 when she had first mailed me seeking help. She was 21, a commerce student from Karnal whose parents were getting her forcefully married. She wanted to study, work and live on her own terms. I always start off with questions that make the concerned person comfortable so that they can open up. She was an Arijit Singh fan, loved Hum Saath Saath Hain[1]and was taking online courses for pursuing e-commerce. She talked at length about how conservative family was but she always wanted to start something on her own, and be a businesswoman. Marriage was not even on her mind but her parents were forcing her to. That was the first session on call. During the second session, she told me that her father had married again after expelling her mother out of the house. Her mother lived with her parents now and had not kept in touch with her since then. That incident was pretty recent, and she had a torrid time facing her father’s new wife who was hardly 3–4 years older than her. I thought for a moment that perhaps she was exaggerating everything but later she showed me wedding pictures of her father’s latest marriage. She knew there was no way out but just wanted to know how to deal with it. I asked her three questions: She had no answers to any one of them. Subsequently, in the fourth session, I asked her that maybe she should prove to her father that she can handle business and ask him to give her some time and money. She was able to somehow convince her uncle, who in turn convinced her father to give her 5 months and initial investment to start an online business. By this time, she told me that she was in a relationship around a year ago. Things did not work out, and that had left a scar on her mind. I told her to prioritize things and focus on what was more important. She was at a stage where she was confident that she would be able to make good use of the time and money, and prove to her father that she could make it big as a businesswoman. We were texting once a day now. She was regularly updating me on how she was setting up her online store for women’s garments. She seemed pretty excited and regularly asked me how she could market it well. She had sold most of her products to her friends, relatives, and inner social circle. For the next three weeks, there was no update from her. I thought perhaps she has gotten too busy with her work. One night at around 2 a.m. she called me. She was all tears. “Brother, I do not know what do! My mother passed away and father is adamant that I should get married as soon as possible. There is no way to escape this hell! Please help me.” We talked for about half an hour, and I calmed her down. I asked her to sleep over it, and we will find some way out of it. She kept the call and till today I have never heard from her. Within a week, her Whatsapp was deactivated. Her Facebook profile vanished and she never replied on mail. I told myself perhaps she accepted her fate and got married. 15th March 2019, I got a call from her uncle. He asked me if I was her boyfriend. I clarified that I was mentoring her and was helping her to set up her online store. He told me that I would have to give a statement on those same terms. I was perplexed as to why. They had got my number from her call records. She had been missing from the past 3 months. Her father had beaten the hell out of her ex-boyfriend doubting that he must have done something to her. Question: Can you do a detailed comparison between Marvel Cinematic Universe and Game of Thrones?
Answer: I will begin this answer by pointing out that I have followed both the franchises ardently. Began with reading ASIOF long ago and started following the MCU when Iron Man 2 came out. Both are not comparable but according to me what really differentiates both of them is the screen time and hence the freedom to explore each character’s arc. Let me start out with a small example. This is Jane Foster, portrayed by Natalie Portman in the MCU. She is the love interest of Thor Odinson. She starred in Thor and Thor: Dark World and has a small cameo in Avengers: Endgame. Her character arc started from Thor and was further strengthened in Dark World, thereafter we only hear about her once or twice in one of the subsequent movies. What happened to her exactly? Why is Thor not with her? Why did not he reach out to her when he was depressed? There is even a scene in Endgame where drunk Thor talks about her nostalgically but despite the entire Avengers saga coming to an end, we don’t have a definitive answer to such questions. This is Talisa Maegyr, played by Oona Chaplin. She is the love interest of Robb Stark. She is shown as a healer working on the battlefield in the “Battle of the Five Kings”. Talisa goes onto comfort Robb when he learns Jaime has been released from prison. They talk about their past, their feeling and eventually marry in secret. However, she is killed during the Red Wedding along with Robb. The character came, the character bonded with fellow characters, the character had an ending. The viewer is never left with any questions as to what happened or why it happened. “Closure” is prioritized even though the character's demise may be not welcomed by many viewers. Take up any character from Thrones world, Jorah Mormont, Samwell Tarly, Euron Greyjoy or even the tiny lass Lyanna Mormont, viewers have closure with each character. Pick up characters like Lady Sif, Justin Hammer, Erik Selvig, Betty Ross, Darcy Lewis, Howard The Duck, The Collector, Jack Rollins and so on, you will see that even though these characters were quite important in an MCU movie, most of us do not even remember their names and what exactly happened to them. I believe this is purely because of the fact that Game of Thrones has an 8 season long run with numerous episodes, and hence it has had more run time to explore lots of characters and do justice to them. Also, different directors and writers on these movies did not help either. you would see the that the Russo directed movies are clearly ahead in these comparisons. Watching the MCU movie is pure fun, but honestly, the writing part with the sidelined characters is off compared to Game of Thrones. Remember, that only in Infinity War did MCU scare the hell out of everyone with a character they had been showcasing from the beginning. I love both Alan Silvestri and Ramin Djawidi as the music composers, but Ramin clearly is the winner. MCU is like a fling with an exotic partner on an island vacation, GOT, on the other hand, is like marriage, you need to be patient and calm to actually enjoy the fruits of a long term relation, forgiving the obstacles on the way. Honestly, MCU is good for a fun day where you want to feel hopeful and badass. GOT is meant for a binge when you want to feel sad about how human emotions can be devastating provided you have the patience to reach the end of Season 1. I love both of them, for if everything was the same, where would be the variety in life!

Question: What are some of the most amazing World War 2 stories?
Answer: March 31, 1943 Second lieutenant Owen Baggett and his B-24 squadron were ordered to take down a bridge in Burma. Baggett’s squadron was stationed in British India at the time of briefing. [1] Enroute to their target, the B-24s were intercepted by Ki-43 and they were slightly outnumbered. Baggett’s plane caught fire after several shots to his fuel tank. the crew and Baggett were forced to bail out. During the Parachute descent, the crew was heavily attacked at, and the B-24 they had bailed out of exploded as it hit the ground. Two of Baggett’s crew were killed during the parachute descent. Baggett, cleverly acted as if he was dead while still in the air, hanging onto his parachute. A Ki-43 plane came close to Baggett and slowed down. The pilot opened his canopy to check Baggett’s condition. Baggett used his pistol immediately and fired four shots at the pilot. The plane stalled, and moments later crashed to the ground. Baggett survived the parachute descent and was held as a prisoner by the Japanese until the end of the war. He remains, on record, the only man to shoot down an aircraft with a pistol.

Question: What is your review of Shazam! (2019 movie)?

The trailers showed a costume that ridiculed the very idea of sleek looking superheroes and Zachary Levi might have not been the perfect choice, according to many fans. Well, this movie surprises you, makes you laugh, and teaches some nice valuable lessons for the kids as well. One thing DC always surprises me with is the use of references of different universes in their storyline. They do so abundantly in the TV series “The Flash”. From Game of Thrones, Harry Potter, Star Wars, to their own superheroes, this movie is filled with them. The first 10 minutes might make you feel that this is just another cliched origin story; well, it is but it’s more funny and more hilarious. A small kid turning into a full grown superhero might be weird and I was thinking if I was that kid, I would go and buy me some beer; and they actually end up doing that. It’s relatable in many ways because the scenes narrate what we always wanted to do as a kid - buy the best games, have lots of money and so on. Well, that’s just the relatability part. The humour also struck me in a good sense. At places it is dark but it hits the right chords. Zachary Levi, surprisingly, pulls off the character brilliantly. If he looked silly in the trailers, it is because the story demanded him to look so. Delicate relations between foster kids and their fascination with superheroes is what starts off the movie and soon it turns out into “What else can Shazam do?” He constantly keeps learning about his powers and that keeps the plot interesting. Even though he grows into an adult superhero, his mind is still a child’s and that has been narrated realistically. The only drawback, I felt, was that the villain could have been narrated better. Whenever I think DC, I think of the Joker or the Reverse Flash. Sadly, the villain in the movie couldn’t satisfy me much. I am guessing not many people would like how the climax unfolds but it is good in its own way. See it like the way it is meant to be: a kid with adult superpowers, who has no clue what to do with them. It’s like Hancock meets Superman in their adolescent stage and there’s a guest appearance in the end that you will love.

Question: What is the best life advice you would give?
Answer: “When it’s over, it’ll all feel like it never happened.” I was going through clinical depression and I had no clue about it. I ran away from the forces and I had no clue why. My mind was blank and I hardly remembered anything and when I came to senses it was too late. I had a graduation degree which was useless outside the military circles. I was wanted by civil and military police for more than a year, and I hadn’t even done anything wrong. My own loved ones in the family called me a traitor. Some of my friends stopped talking to me when I asked them for help. My family was ashamed of me. And through all this, I was in severe clinical depression and I was hellbent at not taking medication or consulting someone. A year later, I gathered the courage to face my demons and went back. I was kept in close arrest till my trials were on. I was alone in a single room for more than 4 months. I had become insane during that time. When I was discharged from duty, I had no clue what I would do with my life. I was 25 without a job, without any skills and to kill my boredom in close arrest, I had written my second novel in captivity. I never realised that I had developed an imaginary friend to talk to during my stint of close arrest. I had developed a new mental syndrome and I was completely unaware. I felt guilty for what I had done even though most of it was not under my control. A year down the line, I was engaged to a beautiful girl, my imaginary friend was rarely seen and I had a job as a content writer. I was doing various online courses to develop new skills and I had started ignoring what people had to say about me. Soon, my imaginary friend came back. The girl I loved left me, and I was back to square one. I had had enough of life, I was trying to control my guilt by helping a few people clear their defence exams and suddenly, I did not even have the courage to do that. I was 27, had left my job recklessly, financially broke and a debt on my head. I wanted to prove to everyone that I was neither a traitor nor a loser. I just wanted to be normal. Today, I’m 29. I have made writing my second life. I want to tell people how not to live their lives and I help people understand the importance of mental health. I guide and encourage people to join the forces. I have done everything I wanted to do in the last two years. The amount I have traveled and made new friends is quite unbelievable honestly. I cleared all the debts, and now I savour a normal life where I stay with my parents and lead my life on my own terms. Two months ago, I was speaking at a Tedx event near my town. My parents had come for the very first time to attend it. I could say they were quite proud of me, that day. Probably, they had never thought my life would turn out like this but howsoever it is, now no one can tell them that their son is a traitor. People don’t know or remember the life I have been through, sometimes even I forget. All they see is a good writer, adventure freak biker and a successful author. My imaginary friend laughs at all this chaos at times, although I have made a pact with him to stay calm always. Hardly a few people know I’m partially schizophrenic. What I want to say is: “When it’s over, it’ll all feel like it never happened.” Provided you don’t stop on the road. Nobody remembers your ordeals, someday even you won’t but getting to that stage takes a lot of ass-whooping. If an idiot like me can survive, you can pretty well survive.

Question: Why are breakups so painful?
Answer: The body and the mind loves being in the comfort zone, a zone where a routine is being followed, a zone where everything seems in order. Break the pattern and the mind loses it. When you breakup, these are some of the questions that arise usually in our mind. Trust me, I too had all these questions running in my mind, and it is pretty natural to have them. Most of us turn into a revenge plot, some of us like drowning ourselves in pain and some us just laugh it off trying to improve ourselves. All these actions are the mind trying to cope up with a new zone it is experiencing, a situation where the person who meant the world to you, is no longer a part of your plans. As I said, we do not like change and part of the process of making breakups less painful is accepting change. The main reason it is painful is we start questioning our worth that leads to low self-esteem. We are so used to hearing the good stuff about us from our partners, and suddenly it vanishes. Secondly, just the feeling that our partner would be sharing the same bond with someone else in the future burns us up from inside. This is the main cause for low self-esteem where we start asking ourselves if we were not good enough for them. Why did I have to suffer? I gave my best shot. If you were true to the relation, you need not blame yourself at all. Be happy that it happened sooner. Things would have been much worse if you were married or if your social circle was more used to you as a couple. Will I get someone else in my life? You will, but not in the state you are. Trust me, no one wants a partner who is still hung on a previous breakup. There will be someone as weird as you somewhere, give yourself time. What do I do with all the memories and dreams that we shared? Cherish the memories, the silly fights, the cuddles, the impulsive outings, the hugs and everything. You enjoyed them when it happened so don’t cry about it. Why am I so unlucky? You’re unlucky because you’re an idiot who has not understood life. You’d be lucky if you accept what life has thrown at you. If someone does not want to be with you, so be it. The only thing you can force in life and be successful with it, is shit, love for sure cannot be forced onto someone. In the first place, if you are not ready or willing for a relationship, don’t get into one for the sake of it. If you are into one, and don’t feel like staying, do so in a gentle manner. I remember when all this happened to me, my parents were really devastated. She was very nice to them, and had talked with them and shared a lot of meals together. My parents had started seeing her as own daughter. When it ended, howsoever it did, she didn’t even bother informing them or even meeting me once. It was just done on a message. Best Cute Friend She killed it in Dear Zindagi, and she kills it again amongst the huge cast ensemble. Yashaswini Dayama is one for the future. Best BFF I feel this role was written for Kalki by the writers. The rich spoilt brat who would do anything to get her man. Best Money Lender Vijay Raaz replays his role from Delhi Belly and his scenes with Jim Sarbh are just pure gold. Best CCTV Victim Arjun Mathur surprise you in every scene. Best Ex-Employee Natasha Singh as the production head will show you another side of being an honest employee and her tryst with financial conflicts. Question: Can you write any beautiful, but short, love story?
Answer: I could smell alcohol everywhere that night. There were bodies swarming around everywhere holding a glass or a bottle. I hardly knew most of them, so I preferred a small corner on the balcony with a few of my team members. It was one of those days when the entire office was excited for the party but soon realised it was a disaster because most of them were passing out one by one. I held a bottle of beer in my hand and was being part of random conversations striking my patented fake smile. That’s what I do, I drink and I pretend that I like people. I felt I was on a bridge connecting people whom I knew and strangers who worked at my office. I was pushing my side to the familiar side, and honestly I am at the age of my life where I judge young people who get drunk and act silly. That makes me feel old, really old but then she walked in suddenly towards the corner. That’s when the havoc began but the thing is I am too adept at handling such havocs. I heard her talking, laughing at the silliest jokes, hysterically couldn’t look at her because I prefer being this shy kid from inside. She left our group and my eyes drooped but she was back again after a few minutes. We were all standing in a huddle and having a conversation that befits the drunken ones. I don’t remember what it was, but it was something that she had a strong opinion about. The bar counter closed soon as we realised most of the interns had lost their bearings of the world, and I had just picked up my last pint of beer. People were leaving slowly and I walked towards the food kiosk to grab some food to catalyse the beer in my belly. I saw her leaving and I smiled, I remembered that I had never really talked to her much, not even the customary greetings, not the fake smile I am so good at. We would have seen eye to eye for a good 40 seconds over the period of one year. I showed my beer to her and nodded, she smiled back. Someone came up from behind her and started talking to her so I turned away. I checked my phone if I had got any mails or calls. As I turned back, she was standing there with her Silk Road smile. She hugged me tightly and kissed me on my cheek. “You’re a nice kid.” “Kid?” I replied. “Yes,” she replied and left the place. I guess that was sufficient enough for me in that very moment. Sometimes, just the idea of the other person acknowledging your existence means the world to us. Why do we need to spoil it by bringing in our complex human emotions in between? Sometimes, it’s just beautiful to have had a moment of existence in eyes that otherwise never bother to accept your pretence. It’s not about the touch, it’s not about the embrace, it’s about that tiny smile on her face that told me that she knew.

Question: Can you write a short story with two meanings?
Answer: Black shirt, unkept hair, a staunch aroma and a cotton trouser that hadn’t touched detergents in ages adorned a man sitting quietly on the bench outside the bar. The year was 1958, and he had just left everything he owned behind. 11 years since Independence, and he was still unheard of. His sense of pride and freedom was entangled, he spoke only when spoken to. He had a missing thumb on his right hand, a broken nasal septum and a golden molar teeth. He had all the money in the world but his scars from the prisoner camp made him feel poor. The government had earmarked him for a covert operation in Baluchistan years ago, and because of him a lot of intel poured in during the 1948 war. Now, he was just a mismatch in the society. He had seen war, he had seen people on both sides of the border before and after partition. His fluent Urdu and Punjabi had helped him survive his espionage. He sat outside the bar in Calcutta waiting for a weapons dealer from East Pakistan. His family had been burnt alive in Mathura and his only friend was now a cabinet minister in the government. For what was worth, his only friend was his denial of government policies on both sides of the border. He had realised it on day one of his espionage that everything was about gaining power and sitting on the chair eventually during a war, even if it is only for a few days, and that is why he enjoyed lonely benches. A tall man walked out wearing a grey overcoat. His hair was greyish with a tinge of brown that reeked of poor quality Henna. He stood up from the bench and took out his Beretta, paused for a while, took a deep breathe and felt the trigger hard enough to penetrate the weapons dealer’s spine. There was no one around and the live band inside the bar was too loud. He walked away staring at the dead man on the pavement. Another man down, another propaganda by a government successfully propagated and another sin encumbered on an assassin’s soul. For years, people like him have been trained and kept undercover to carry out such minuscule operations. The reward is nullified absence of conscience in such young men. Governments on both sides of the border emulate the same. Israel, USA, Russia, even African nations have a pool of such men whom nobody has heard of. By the time, they taste their first kill, they all realise the truth. It is all about who will be in power when the elections come. Black hoodie, a white underlying tee and a torn jeans that talked about his stint in Belarus decorated a man who was sitting just outside Sonagachi in Kolkatta. Everywhere, there were posters of the state’s leaders. The man was silently waiting for a booth capturer from Bangladesh. Elections were coming again and this time there was a new propaganda. The year was 2019.

Question: If you could change one thing about Indian society, what would it be?
