She has been going out of her way to find family oriented and simple girls for me, which in all honesty is the complete opposite of me in every single parallel universe as well. Now, the problem is that I cannot hurt my mother by saying an outright “no”. She has lectured me on how this is the right age to get married for days and days together, and honestly she will never understand that I feel I have so much more to do in life and I’m not meant for this average-get-married-get-settled and make your mother a granny style of living. I had promised her that if I come across someone I like, I will tell her but that never happened so from the past two months she has been showing me photographs and bringing home a few families as well. Now, even though I’m a rogue in my mind, in front of my parents, just to keep them happy, I pretend to be a decent guy. The first question the girl’s parents always ask is, “How much do you earn and is this your own house?” I lose it there but I look at my mother and just keep quiet. Questions that follow are, “When are you planning to buy a car and do you smoke or drink?” I obviously have to lie about that with a fake smile. Now, after a few more questions, my mother starts asking for the horoscope and the girl’s parents start showing more interest. It’s a code-red situation for me and then I suddenly come up with a question that changes the game in my favour. “Does your daughter suffer from any health issues?” “No, she is healthy as a horse. What about you?” “I was clinically depressed for three years.” Suddenly, their faces turn upside down, and later on the call, they outrightly refuse the proposal. I have done the same thrice. Once over messaging to a prospective girl, and once more to the girl’s brother who had come to meet me first. I wish I didn’t have to meet all these prospective brides but to keep my mother happy, I have agreed for some time. Thanks to Indian society which has no respect and room for people with mental health issues, I get away always. And as much as I wish for it to change, I know it never will. Long live my country.

Question: How did Manchester United manage to beat PSG?
Answer: It was a miracle, nonetheless! Beating PSG at their home after being 2–0 down in a Champions League fixture with a 2nd string team. Nobody, not even most of the fans, would have given United a sniff of victory, but as things turned out, it was a night when Manchester conquered Paris. The first goal within 2 minutes would have calmed the United nerves, but nevertheless it was a grave mistake by the PSG Defence. Lukaku was quick to pounce on it, and for a while it seemed like United could pull off a great victory, until PSG came together and dominated possession for a good 10–15 minutes. Their goal was sheer brilliance, with United’s Defence looking all over the place. Despite playing a back 5, there was no communication, and Bailly was letting people run behind him. Bernant scores for PSG, but it was more to do with Mbappe’s cross and his innovativeness. Solksjaer was quick to spot the chink in the armor and replaced Bailly with the 19 year old Dalot. Young moved back and United played a more conventional back 4 with Dalot making runs along the wings. Even then PSG looked more likely to score. They dominated the possession and even though United got one more goal thanks to some poor keeping from Buffon, PSG always looked in control. By half time, they were still leading on aggregate. The second half started on the same note with PSG dominating the possession. It was 70–30 in terms of possession by the 75th minute. United were forced to stay in their own half while Verrati, Draxler, Dani Alves and co. displayed some excellent passing streaks. United were strong in defence at this time, and were patiently waiting to counter which was not happening. Di Maria scored but was caught offside. Mbappe was one on one with De Gea but he couldn’t get past the Spaniard and Smalling came to the rescue. It always looked like PSG would score anytime and United were just piggybacking in search of that one goal. That was until in last 5 minutes of the stipulated time Dalot attempted a shot from outside the box. VAR was taken and it was found that the ball had hit the defender’s arm. Even though it was a very controversial decision, the penalty was awarded and Rashford scored from the spot. Extra time of 3 minutes was over but the referee extended the play upto 99th minute to compensate for the time wasted in VAR decision. I think United won because once they took out Bailly, their defence was rock solid. Smalling, Lindelof and Shaw were on point with their offside traps, and handling Mbappe and Di Maria. All the three United goals were mostly based on PSG’s mistakes, but they were converted. PSG however missed a lot of chances and couldn’t convert their possession. And as Solksjaer said later, “We believed.” So good to see the United way of playing football.

Question: Have you ever come across or interacted with a Pakistani Intelligence Operative?
Answer: Everything you do on the Internet is monitored and tracked by intelligence agencies. Especially, if you are related to the armed forces in one way or the another. Hence, defense personnel are always advised to not reveal their details and post pictures in uniforms. Since the time I started writing columns of aviation and answering here on Quora, I was sure something someday would definitely pop up. Back in the days when I was an officer, we had a lot of cases where beautiful girls sent random requests to young officers, started chatting and tried to take out sensitive information. Sometimes, they even visited the operational units to meet the officers. Even the slightest of information leaked can be useful to them. The most prominent ones carrying out such operations are PIO’s (Pakistani Intelligence Operatives). These have been pretty active since the advent of social media has started. Usually, they will have pretty pictures on their profile which cannot be reverse searched on the internet. Their mutual friend list will have people involved with the defense forces in some way or the other. And they chat with you like a real person and try to lure you in by chatting for days together, and then attempt to leak out some vital information. A few months ago, a friend request came to me on Facebook. The moment a pretty girl messages me, I get suspicious. I know myself and I know pretty girls don't send requests to random guys on the internet. She had no friends at all, and she had a lot of privacy settings on her profile so I was not able to see mutual friends as well. I accepted the request but never messaged at all. A few months later, she randomly started commenting on my posts which again was very dubious to me. One day, out of the blue she messaged me and told me that she loved my writings on Quora, and she enjoys the funny one-liners I post on Facebook. She messaged from time to time, and I kept it to a normal conversation. Then, one day when I announced that I will be addressing a few students in Pune, she messaged me that she is flying down from Dubai to Pune for the weekend as well and that she wanted to meet. I told her that I will be staying at the Officer’s Mess inside College of Military engineering, and she can come and grab a few drinks with me and my friends. She did not respond and did not message me again for a month or so. Suddenly, out of the blue, she told me she wants to have a phone call with me, and that she will call me. Again, she disappeared for a few days and came back apologizing for the same. By this time I was sure what was happening. Her Facebook had just a few posts, and for a pretty girl to have only a few likes on her pictures was really very suspicious. Next time she messaged, I joked that it is a fake profile and that caught her off guard. I called her Mr. Rathore which infuriated her more. In between, she used to send me her pictures trying to ascertain that she was not a fake profile as well. Things started clearing out when she asked me my opinion of the ongoing airstrikes and the terrorist strikes. She wanted to know generally how the people of India feel and why don’t I write about it clearly, as I might be aware of so many facts being from a defense background. I reported the profile and informed my coursemates about the same. Many more fake profiles had been active during the same period, and even some of my friends had been chatting with the same profile. Thankfully, everyone was clever enough not to divulge away any details. A list was circulated soon, and potential PIOs were earmarked for everyone to know. If you or your friends or family are involved with the defense forces, you will surely be targetted. Keep your pants intact, and be smart. A lot of such cases have happened in the past. and a lot of information has also been retrieved by the PIOs. So, stay safe and stay smart. PS: She hasn't replied from the past 3 days and I am so sad.

Question: What is the history of Pakistan-administered Kashmir?
Answer: Let us roll back a bit in time, way back to the time when Mughals were ruling India. Akbar had conquered Kashmir and ended the Kashmiri Muslim rule. It was a seat of high importance for the Mughals, and soon even Shahjahan made it into a top-level province with a vital seat at Srinagar.[1] As the Mughal dynasty faded, Durrani empire’s Ahmed Shah took over Kashmir from 1751 after defeating Ahmed Shah Bahadur. By 1819 or so, the Durrani empire fell to the Sikh army of Ranjit Singh. The Kashmiris had been tortured and humiliated a lot under the Durrani rule, so they welcomed the Sikh regime with open hands. The rule under Sikhs was, however, more aggravating in terms of a number of Anti-Muslim laws where cow slaughter was banned, and even the Jama Masjid in Srinagar was closed down. The taxes were also very high and cultivation took a huge backlash, even forcing many Kashmiris to migrate to Punjab. As fate had it, a famine struck Kashmir, and Sikhs were forced to bring down taxes and be more friendly with the local cultivators. A lot of western travels had started visiting Kashmir and writing about the plight of the locals. This also led to the popularity of the local Kashmiri shawls worldwide. Gulab Singh, who had risen through ranks in the Sikh troops was soo appointed as the “Raja of Jammu”. He went on to conquer Rajouri, Kargil, and Ladakh and thereby strengthening their presence in the valley. [2] Drafted by a treaty and a bill of sale, and constituted between 1820 and 1858, the Princely State of Kashmir and Jammu (as it was first called) combined disparate regions, religions, and ethnicities: to the east, Ladakh was ethnically and culturally Tibetan and its inhabitants practiced Buddhism; to the south, Jammu had a mixed population of Hindus, Muslims, and Sikhs; in the heavily populated central Kashmir valley, the population was overwhelmingly Sunni Muslim, however, there was also a small but influential Hindu minority, the Kashmiri brahmins or pandits; to the northeast, sparsely populated Baltistan had a population ethnically related to Ladakh, but which practised Shia Islam; to the north, also sparsely populated, Gilgit Agency, was an area of diverse, mostly Shi'a groups; and, to the west, Punch was Muslim, but of different ethnicity than the Kashmir valley. After the Indian Rebellion of 1857, in which Kashmir sided with the British, and the subsequent assumption of direct rule by Great Britain, the princely state of Kashmir came under the suzerainty of the British Crown. Hari Singh was the reigning Monarch of Kashmir when India gained Independence. There were two major parties at that time in the princely state. National Conference and the Muslim Conference. Both of them had opposing views, while one wanted to be part of India, the other wanted to be of Pakistan. The Muslim conference was quite popular in the Jammu region and the Nation Conference in Kashmir. While Hari Singh wanted to remain an independent state, the Muslims of Western Jammu Province (present-day PoK) and a few others were adamant on being part of Pakistan. Late in 1947, a revolt broke put against Hari Singh and western districts of Poonch, Muzzafarabad and Mirpur declared a provisional Azad Kashmir government in Rawalpindi. This government soon fizzled out when their leader “Mr. Anwar” was arrested in Srinagar. A second provisional government was also soon proclaimed. In October 1947, thousands of Pashtun tribesmen stormed into Jammu and Kashmir to liberate it from Maharaja Hari Singh. Hari Singh’s forces were too weak to withstand the same and soon he asked India for assistance. India, in return, agreed to help provided he signed the Instrument of Accession (accession to India). Pakistan also intervened soon when Indian troops were airlifted to Srinagar. War resumed until areas of control were established along the line which is known in the present times as “Line of Control”. India approached the United Nations for a resolution and a plebiscite was suggested which never took place. In 1949, a ceasefire took place and the Pakistani government divided the PoK into two separate political units. Azad Jammu & Kashmir Gilgit-Baltistan During the 1972 Shimla Agreement between the two countries, “Line of Control” was bought into existence. The line has since remained disputed, unchanged and an issue that seems to have taken an eternity to get resolved.

Question: How would Indian Army react to the recent terrorist attack on CRPF in Pulwama, Kashmir ?
Answer: Have you ever been in a situation where no matter how honest your efforts are, you end up being on the wrong side? We all have been there, the fact is that sometimes you cannot please the very people you have been striving to please to. Let me rewind a bit to last year when I was staying with one of my coursemates in Anantnag. It was a secure army unit that was not even visible from outside. I was en route to Srinagar from Kanyakumari on my bike. I got really late after Udhampur and by the time I crossed Jawahar Tunnel, it had become dark. My coursemate was constantly calling me to advise not to get off the highway at any cost. When I reached, I asked him if we could go outside for tea. He laughed initially and told me that army personnel do not venture out of the unit alone unless there is a convoy. It is as good as inviting death. I asked him then that how does it feel to be on duty to protect the very same people who are trying to kill you. There was one army doctor who was in his room that time and he replied. “I see casualties every day here. Some of them are soldiers and some of them civilians as well. We never differentiate and focus on saving lives first.” I pointed out that the medical facilities available in the unit were inadequate and he was doing a great job. He replied with a lot of depth in his voice. “Srinagar is hardly 10–15 minutes by a helicopter from here. By road, it takes more than an hour. Choppers don’t fly because there is a threat that they might be shot down when flying so low.” “Even when civilian lives are involved?” I asked. “They only see that it’s an Indian army chopper, nothing else matters in this area. Sometimes, soldiers land up here with wounds given to them by civilians as well.” My coursemate replied. “When there were floods here, a few months back, the entire unit was drowned and still we were helping out everyone possible. Indian army saved the day and for a moment, the locals understood that we are only trying to help out. I do agree there are some casualties sometimes which we do not intend to, but that’s part of war and we try to avoid that as much as possible.” the doctor added. “Then what’s the solution?” I asked. “People here have no clue what is development. They are cut off from the world. It is very easy to brainwash them, especially the young ones. A lot of the blame goes to the governments that have been in power. This region needs a leader who understands that giving the right education and proper infrastructure would change everything.” We talked and argued a lot but I understood that the two people in the room had been serving for more than 3 years in the valley and knew the situation much better. Mind you, my coursemate was a Kashmiri himself but understood how sensitive the situation was. He wasn’t in the forces to serve the country, he was passionate for the uniform and didn’t want successive generations to be bought up the way he was. The next day I went to Srinagar and then to Ladakh. On the way back in Sonamarg, a local asked me to drop him till Anantnag on my bike. The only reason he asked me was that my bike has a registration from South India. I realised how much he hated the army for the tension in the valley. His reasons were random but it was clear he was going along with what he thought was right. Along the highway, a convoy of some 15–20 buses of CRPF and Indian Army protected by armoured vehicles was travelling ahead of us. All along the stretch, one side of the highway was blocked, and there were soldiers patrolling every 50 metres. This infuriated my pillion rider more and he told me that this was a daily affair here. I dropped him at a junction and didn’t tell him I was ex-armed force as most of my coursemates had adviced me not to do so anywhere, especially in South Kashmir. I believe in a three-fold approach to the present situation here. I honestly believe that education and development is the long term weapon. Everything South of Jawahar Tunnel is peaceful because people there have seen development. I have lost more than 12 coursemates, juniors and seniors I personally knew in the last 2 years. Every time I hear the news, my blood boils but the strategic leadership as of now needs to understand consequences and drawbacks. Hasty decisions more often than not lead to more repercussions. And as common citizens, we can do one simple act to justify all the sacrifices our soldiers make. Do not spread hate and be a rightful citizen. We can sit and pretend there is no war, or we can sit and pretend we are ready to lose more lives. Fact is, we need a fine balance between the two from both the government and the opposition. Trust me, the army knows what it needs to do. Revenge looks good in movies only, what we need is a permanent solution that glorifies all the martyrs in the valley. We can’t afford to lose more lives because of misplaced religious values, poor governance and social media outrage by people who have no clue what’s happening in the valley. Jai Hind!

I soon plan on adopting a few more of them for who does not need unconditional love in this cruel world. Thank you Brover, this is me appreciating your presence in my life.

Question: Can you write an intense story about a man and a woman trapped in a room?
Answer: It was raining outside and one could hear the tiniest drops of water hit the walls of the room that was isolated completely on top of the hill. Ironically, there were two more people inside the room who were shedding teardrops as well. Sion, the 32-year-old construction worker from Andamans had been locked inside the room with his ex-wife Katriel, a quality analyst from Daman. Two days ago, when both of them went to sleep, things seemed spick and span. However, when they woke up, they found themselves in this haunted room. There were 10 dead bodies inside the room, 5 of them male and the other 5 female suggesting the fact that there were 5 more estranged couples in the room before them. In the middle of the room that smelled of sulfur, hung a rope on which a small piece of paper read, “Apologise from the heart or be dead by your soul.” It had been more than 24 hours and they had not spoken a word to each other. Sion was crying as he feared death and Katriel was in tears because she was about to propose a younger man in her office the evening she was mysteriously abducted. In the air, tension loomed in many forms, and in the vicinity, rainfall made the aura even more dreadful. There was no running away from the hatred they had for each other, and even the fear of death could not break their egos. “I am sorry, just let me go now and live my life.” Katriel sobbed. “You think I set this all up to take revenge? Why do you always assume things about me?” Sion shouted at the top of his voice which perched through the water droplets out of the tiny outlet on the southern wall. “I went to sleep peacefully because I was finally in love with a sensible man. You would not even let me live my life. Only you can go to such an extent to set me up here, Sion.” “I have no clue why I am here or why, of all the people, you had to be here.” “Stop fooling around, Sion. I know you way too well.” “You think I am a psychotic freak who would lock himself up in a dark room with no food or water along with some dead bodies so that I can get an apology from you.” “So, what do you want?” Katriel asked assertively. “I want to be over with you. Ever since you left me, all I have wanted to do is be peaceful with myself but I cannot. I miss your clothes on the floor when I wake up, I miss those burnt toasts you made for me. I miss surprising you by coming early from work, I miss leaning on your shoulder and abusing my boss, I miss every single freckle on your cheeks and even though I have told myself a 1000 times that you have left me, I still keep missing those things. Why did you have to leave when everything was so perfect? What joy did you get?” “Oh, shut up, Sion. I know you inside out. You were the one who spoilt it. You had made me the center of all your worries, pain, and conflicts. You were like a small baby who did not know how to take care of himself. Rectifying you was not my job. “ “I behaved that way because you felt like home, someone who would love me the way I was. I never complained about what you did. Your late night outings, your absence from home for days without even a call, your mood swings, I thought it was always about one of us being sane no matter what happened. you taught me how to love, and then suddenly one day you walked away leaving behind a letter. Was it so easy for you?” “Easy? I wept for days together, you moron! I was so used to holding you and sleeping, I had to buy hundreds of pillows until one of them felt like you. I was at my mother’s place for months together not moving out.” “Then, why did you do it?” “It was the right thing to do, Sion.” “Who made you the judge of right and wrong for us, wasn’t it always supposed to be a mutual decision?” “I don’t know. I never doubted that you loved me but love sometimes is not enough.” “Love is always enough.” Sion sighed. “Look what love made you do. You haven’t changed at all. You are still the emotional fool you were.” “I was your emotional fool.” “Oh, stop with it, already Sion.” “I am really sorry, Katriel if I put you in a situation where you felt you deserved better. All I was trying to do was to love you the best way I knew, and to be honest that is the only thing I know how to do.” Sion broke down on his knees and sobbed like an infant. The rainfall continued outside and so did the emotional commotion inside. “I am not sorry, Sion. I did love you but at that moment it was the right decision for me. I decided I am really not concerned with you, thereafter.” “I guess, we both will turn out to be like these dead bodies if that is the case.” “I would rather be dead than to apologize for something I did not even do. Love is not everything in life. You gave me the best days of my life but you were also pulling me down, I did not want to babysit you all my life.” “I have loved you so much that I will respect your decision, and silently wait.” “If this is how it ends, then so be it. I do not want to give you false hopes by apologizing because I do not mean it.” The rainfall stopped and so did the tears. Both of them sat against the wall on the opposite walls unable to see each other in the darkness. hours passed by but no one spoke a word. As tiny photons of sunlight slowly peeped through into the room, Sion saw Katriel sleeping on the floor. He wondered if things could have been different but they were not. Katriel had gone into a deep sleep. Now it was just a matter of time before both of them succumbed to hunger, thirst and mental fatigue. The dead bodies on the other side of the room lay still, perhaps ego had killed them too.

Question: How do you know if someone's really your friend?
Answer: We all hail from different backgrounds, share different opinions and most importantly we all are financially differently abled. We have different work ethics, different cultural backgrounds, and different priorities. However, there is one thing that is common to all of us. No, not the human spirit or our basic human anatomy. It is time. We all have 24 hours only. Some of us utilize it in a better manner and some of us probably do not. However, if someone can give you their time when you need it the most, he truly is a good friend. Anyone can sit with you and drink, hang out with you and be there when the times are good but only a true friend will give you time out of his 24 hours when you require a shoulder to rest your head. Parking is around 8 kms away from the statue and from there only buses organised by the government for the statue ply. Question: What is your review of Aquaman (2018 movie)?
Answer: Remember this Aquaman cosplay by Raj in The Big Bang Theory? Well, thanks to Jason Momoa and James Wan, Aquaman will probably be the most badass superheroes you come across now. Amidst all the hype and speculations regarding the trailer for Avengers: Endgame, most of the superhero fans totally forgot this visual spectacle by James Wan. I have always loved his tight camera angles since Conjuring and Insidious, and his ability to build a movie slowly towards a superb climax. What James does with Aquaman is that he gives you three climaxes, and each feel perfectly aligned with the storyline. Although, many would argue that it feels like Thor:Ragnarok and Black Panther, I'd still give you 5 reasons why Aquaman totally works and might lead to a DC revamp. Cast: Jason Momoa was born to play Aquaman, there is no doubt about that. Most of the full scenes are made exciting by his mere presence. Along with Amber Heard, Nicole Kidman, Patrick Wilson, Willem Dafoe, Dolph Lundgren and other actors, the cast ensemble looks spot on. Action Scenes: Although, I wasn’t much impressed with initial submarine sequence, the action sequence in Sicily, Italy just blew my mind. James Wan has his camera panning in and out and with some great action directors and VFX, the face off between Black Manta and Aquaman was a treat to watch. Visual Imagery: The underwater scenes are a visual spectacle. The particular scene where they jump off a boat into the trench of the dead is just orgasmic. All the war scenes in Atlantis and the attack on Brine have been brilliantly executed. Plot: Even though the plot derives from a lot of cliched superhero movies, the narration is what makes it different. The flashbacks are appropriately placed, and the overlapping dialogues in some scenes make it more endearing specially the one where Aquaman talks about how his father goes to the dock everyday to wait for his mother. Hope: The movie does not divulge much information about what time period is the story set in, is it after Justice League events, or even before Batman VS Superman, except for a few instances where Mera divulges a few facts. I am hoping this might revamp the whole DC universe, with Flashpoint in making, and this gives us a whole new storyline probably where the entire storyline to this point in the DC universe is ignored. As much as I am a MCU fan, I don’t want DC to suffer because DC comics were the one I grew up on. It would be wonderful to see both these franchises make brilliant movies together. Aquaman surely gives Comic book fans that hope. All hail the king!

Answer: Listen, sometimes we give our all We would take a bullet And often they would be Behind the gun aimed at you Skins splashed, Tyres rammed Eyes popped up because of All the popped up pills Trying to gather your heart From the floor in spills In your mind The Flashback stills Them conquered hills And the bullet you fired at me Halfway there Ready for its kills . . . . Spit my pain in a bowl And spin it and watch it freeze And I thought I thought of you Every time I had a sneeze Cold beers that lay in me And the empty bottles Along with the spills on the floor I marvel you, bitch Thought you were a superhero All you had was a loud pitch A fraction nonzero, null & void From Delhi to Detroit They talk about how you Fussed and Ditched Fear the lord The bullet you fired Is right at my temple Forehead sweating I am going to die . . . . Paradise Lost Now I feel like a mouse On the pad you moved around But my keyboard allows me to live Review me and you’ll find errors Because of you, them and they And everyone who ignored My friendly “Hey” I’m coping this bullet you fired You stand behind the barrel Laughing at my agony Like the little pink pony . . . . Oh, I forgot to tell you I would have taken a bullet for you There’s a reason why I’m bulletproof, baby Bullets can’t kill me It was just to get through to you Every time you said “No” I heard a “Yes” Built that way I am In wilderness In ruins of madness In churches of illness In temples of dullness In mosques of sadness The bullet you fired at me Has fallen in shame I will live again Come baby, be my witness!
